Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build
 Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Nov 25, 2026 � @Saikat

 TL;DR

 Build Seedsong, a calm browser "sound garden". A recursive function grows a glowing
 fractal tree, and the call tree itself becomes the music. The trunk is the drone, the main
 boughs are the chord progression, branches carry the melody, twigs add ornaments,
 leaves ring as bells, and every return resolves a phrase.
 The user picks a mood, shapes the seed, watches it grow, and downloads the song. The
 name is a working title; rename it freely.

 Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tone.js for audio, Canvas 2D for visuals, Radix UI
 primitives for accessible controls, Vitest + Playwright for tests, GitHub Pages for the
 live demo.
 Where the points are: relaxation/UX (35%) plus musical quality (25%) is 60% of the
 score. Put most hours there, not into extra features.
 Method: drop the starter kit into an empty repo (CLAUDE.md, spec, skills, subagents,
 logging hooks), then run the phase prompts in order. Each phase is plan build 
 verify (tests + browser screenshots) you listen commit.
 Clock (GMT+6): working skeleton with export before you sleep (about 04:00), sleep
 until 09:00, polish all day, feature freeze 18:30, submit by 21:00. The hard deadline is
 22:00.
 Five things decide the score:
 1. It sounds beautiful on the first click. Every note is locked to a scale, timbres are soft,
 reverb is long, and a limiter stops harsh peaks. No random bleeps.
 2. The first minute feels like a ritual. A headphones hint, one Begin tap, then the tree
 grows in sync with the music.
 3. Recursion is visible and audible. A live call-stack "recursion lens" shows each call as it
 plays. A Wander (depth-first) vs Bloom (breadth-first) toggle lets people hear the
 difference.
 4. Export works every time. Offline-rendered WAV, plus MP3, MIDI and cover art,
 covered by an end-to-end test.

 Page 1 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 5. The AI logs are complete. Hooks record every prompt and response automatically.
 Missing logs can get you disqualified.

 Where the points are

 Source: the official Hub's Quest Epoch 1 brief (evaluation section)

 How you feel using it (35%) and how it sounds (25%) decide 60% of the score, so most of
 the build hours go there. Technical execution is only 5%. But the six mandatory
 deliverables are pass/fail, so a broken export or missing control costs far more than 5%.

 Relaxation & UX (35%): the first minute, moods, crossfades, ambience, calm visuals,
 mobile. The judges will feel this before they think about anything else.
 Musical quality (25%): scale-locked harmony that moves, phrases that breathe, a soft
 mix. Listening checkpoints are built into the timeline.
 Creative recursion (15%): won by the idea (the call tree is the musical form) and by
 making it visible. More worlds help less than a clearer mapping.
 Visual design + interaction (20%): one coherent design system and plain-language
 controls, not more screens.
 Technical execution (5%): the tests, CI and clean architecture mostly protect
 everything else from breaking at demo time.
 The judges come from UIU Developers Hub, so most will likely know recursion from a data-
 structures course. A live call-stack view and a code view with the running line highlighted
 make the idea legible to them in seconds.

 Page 2 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Product concept: Seedsong

 Seedsong turns one recursive function into a garden you listen to: plant a seed, watch it
 branch, hear it bloom, keep the song. Tagline for the README hero: "Plant a seed. Watch
 recursion grow. Listen to it bloom."
 Why this concept beats the obvious entries:

 It is the most literal recursive function. branch(length, angle, depth) calls itself,
 so every judge recognises it in one glance. Most rival entries will map Fibonacci
 numbers to random notes.
 The structure is musical, not decorative. A tree already has the shape of a piece of
 music: one root, a few big sections, many small phrases, and endings. Section 4 maps
 each level to a musical role.
 It is calming to watch. Slow growth, swaying branches and glowing blossoms are
 relaxing visuals, and relaxation is the largest rubric line.
 It scales safely. The same engine can later play other recursions as extra "worlds" (an
 L-system garden, a Tower of Hanoi music box) without touching the audio or export
 code.

 The first minute (the judge's first impression)

 1. Landing. Deep twilight gradient, slow drifting motes, the title, and one seed pulsing at
 breathing pace (about 6 breaths a minute). A line reads "Best with headphones". One
 button: Begin. That tap also unlocks browser audio, which browsers require anyway.

 2. 0�8 s. A warm drone fades in. The trunk grows upward with a low note.
 3. 8�60 s. Boughs split into harmony, branches carry the melody, twigs sparkle, and

 leaves open as glowing blossoms with bell tones. The recursion lens prints
 branch(depth 3, length 84, angle 24�) as each note plays.
 4. Ending. The recursion unwinds, the music resolves to the home chord, the tree sways
 gently, and a softly glowing Keep this song button appears.

 Core loop

 Choose a mood shape the seed grow and listen keep (export, share link, save to
 your garden).

 Page 3 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Five moods (one-tap presets)

Each mood sets the scale, tempo, instruments, ambience and colour palette together, so a
non-technical user gets a finished piece in one tap.

Mood Scale and tempo Lead sound Ambience Palette
Dawn peach, rose, gold
Mist D major soft electric piano light birds, on deep indigo
 pentatonic, 60 + warm pad breeze
Rain BPM teal, sage on slate
Garden kalimba pluck + rain
 A minor aqua, cyan on
Deep pentatonic, 56 pad navy
Ocean BPM emerald, moss,
Night slow pad swells + ocean waves firefly yellow
Forest C Lydian, 50 BPM glass bells
 crickets, amber, saffron on
Temple F minor harp-like pluck + stream plum
 pentatonic, 54 low drone
 BPM
 koto-like pluck + wind, distant
 D Yo scale, 48
 BPM singing-bowl drone chimes

Four of the five are pentatonic scales with no semitones, so overlapping notes never
clash. Deep Ocean uses C Lydian; the composer treats its two semitone steps as short
passing notes only.

 Page 4 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Recursion to music: the creative core

 Recursion-to-music mapping � 6 levels and the return rule

 The recursion's structure is the musical structure. Musically a tree is a piece: one key, a
 few sections, many phrases, and endings. Each level of branch() therefore gets a
 different musical job, and each return resolves what its call started. Listeners hear the
 shape of the recursion: phrases inside sections inside the piece, self-similar at every
 scale.

 Page 5 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

The other parameters

Recursion property Musical result

branch length note duration (long boughs, short twigs) and
 loudness

branch angle vs its parent melodic step: left holds, right climbs, jitter adds a
 neighbour note

branch x position stereo position, so the left side of the tree sounds
 on the left

depth register and velocity: deeper is higher and softer

randomness (seeded) gentle timing and velocity humanisation

seed the whole piece: the same seed always grows the
 same song

Two ways to traverse the same tree

 Wander (depth-first, default): the melody climbs one branch to its leaf, comes back,
 and climbs the next, like an improvisation that keeps returning home.
 Bloom (breadth-first): each level plays as a 2-bar phrase, left to right like a harp
 sweep, so the tree blooms level by level from drone to bells.

A toggle lets people hear the difference, which teaches depth-first versus breadth-first
faster than any diagram.

More recursions through the same engine

 L-System Garden (Should): a recursive expand(symbol, depth) grows ferns,
 bushes, Koch snowflakes and dragon curves. [ and ] push and pop the turtle, so
 branches literally start harmony voices and return to the saved pitch.
 Hanoi Music Box (Could): hanoi(n, from, to, via) moves glowing discs; larger
 discs sound lower, each peg has its own timbre, and the smallest disc's every-other-
 move pattern becomes a natural ostinato.

 Page 6 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Features by priority

Ship every Must by 15:00, start Shoulds only once the Musts are verified, and stop adding
features at 18:30. The full spec for each item is in docs/SPEC.md �3 of the starter kit.

Priority Feature What it earns

Must Fractal Grove: depth, branching, spread, Deliverable 1, creative recursion
 length ratio, randomness, asymmetry, seed

Must Composer: fractal form, Wander mode, scale Deliverable 3, musical quality
 lock, cadences, density cap

Must Live audio: five moods, pad/lead/bell/drone Musical quality, relaxation
 voices, reverb, limiter, procedural ambience

Must Canvas tree that grows in sync with the notes, Deliverable 2, visual design
 with glow, particles and sway

Must Transport: play, pause, seek, volume, Deliverable 4, interaction
 regenerate with crossfade

Must Export: offline-rendered WAV with progress, Deliverable 5
 plus MIDI

Must Landing ritual, moods, control drawer, mobile Deliverable 6, relaxation & UX
 layout, keyboard access

Must Live GitHub Pages demo, README, complete Eligibility, technical execution
 AI logs

Should Bloom (breadth-first) mode and a Creative recursion
 Wander/Bloom toggle

Should Recursion lens, code view, depth skyline Creative recursion, visual
 design

Should MP3, cover-art PNG, live session recording Interaction

Should Ambience mixer, breathing companion, sleep Relaxation & UX
 timer, zen mode

Should Share links and a saved-seed "garden" Interaction

Should World 2: L-System Garden Creative recursion

 Page 7 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Priority Feature What it earns

Should Audio QA script, axe accessibility tests, CI Technical execution, musical
 quality

Could World 3: Hanoi Music Box Creative recursion

Could Sampled lead from VSCO 2 CE (public domain, Musical quality
 CC0)

Could Endless Drift: next tree modulates up a fifth Relaxation

Could PWA install and lock-screen controls UX

Could Video export, Bangla UI toggle Interaction, local touch

Won't Accounts, backend, AI-generated audio, Nothing in the rubric
 payments

What "enterprise-ready" means here. It means production quality: a pure, tested core, CI,
a live deploy, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, performance budgets, clean licences and real
documentation. It does not mean enterprise features such as login, databases or admin
panels. Those earn zero rubric points, cost hours and add failure risk, so the plan leaves
them out on purpose.

 Page 8 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Architecture and stack

Seedsong architecture � one score, three outputs

Everything flows from one Score . The recursion and the composer are pure, tested
functions, so the same seed always gives the same piece. The live engine and the exporter
build their instruments with the same createRack() , so the file sounds exactly like
playback. Visuals never schedule audio; they react to note events the audio clock emits
through getDraw() , so sight and sound stay in sync.

Stack (versions checked on npm today)

Layer Choice Version Why
Build Vite + React + TypeScript (strict)
 8.3 / 19.3 / fastest agent-friendly setup;
 7.0 npm create vite now ships
 TypeScript 7 and oxlint

 Page 9 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Layer Choice Version Why

Audio Tone.js 15.1 scheduling, synths, effects,

 offline rendering, recorder

Visuals Canvas 2D built in fast enough for 2,047
 branches, no extra library to
 debug

UI Tailwind CSS + Radix UI primitives 4.3 / 1.8 / 14 accessible sliders, dialogs

 + Motion + Lucide / 1.80 and tabs out of the box

State Zustand 5.1 small, persists settings and

 the garden

Export @tonejs/midi , 2.0 / 1.2 MIDI and MP3; WAV encoder
 written in-house
 @breezystack/lamejs

Tests Vitest + Testing Library, Playwright 5.1 / 1.65 / unit, end-to-end,
 accessibility
 + axe 4.14

Deploy GitHub Actions GitHub Pages free, lives next to the repo
 the judges open

One trap I checked: typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7 yet, so the kit
tells Claude to keep create-vite's oxlint and not add ESLint.

Folder map

src/core (worlds, music, random, url) � src/audio (engine, rack, scheduler, instruments,
ambience) � src/export (offline, wav, mp3 worker, midi, cover, record) � src/viz
(renderer, per-world renderers, particles, camera) � src/ui (components) � src/state �
tests/e2e � scripts . The full tree and interfaces are in SPEC �4.0 and �10.

Budgets

Generate and compose in under 50 ms for the largest tree, 60 fps on desktop and at least
30 on a mid-range phone, under 400 KB of JavaScript gzipped on first load, and no
memory growth across 10 regenerations.

 Page 10 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Sound design

The music sounds intentional for three reasons. Every note is locked to the scale.
Harmony moves through calm, voice-led chords. A proper mix chain keeps everything
soft. The mood table in the concept section sets scale, tempo, timbre and ambience; this
section covers how it is played.

Five rules that separate music from bleeps

 1. Work in scale degrees, never raw pitches. The melody steps through the scale index,
 so a wrong note is impossible by construction.

 2. Harmony must move. One chord per phrase from a calm progression (add9, sus, maj7
 voicings), and each chord is voice-led so the smallest possible movement connects it
 to the last one.

 3. Phrases breathe. Every return from a depth-2 call gets a soft cadence and one beat of
 rest. The piece ends on the home chord with a 10-second tail.

 4. Less is more. At most about 3.5 notes a second, soft velocities, long releases. Silence
 is part of the piece.

 5. Mix it like a record. High-pass everything except drone and bass, use one long reverb
 on a send, then compressor and limiter at -1 dB, aiming for about -18 to -16 LUFS.

Voices and levels

Voice Built from (Tone.js 15) Level Role
Drone two detuned sines, 6 s attack -24 dB the trunk: key and
 root
Pad PolySynth of fat triangles low-pass -18 dB chords per phrase

 with slow LFO chorus -12 to -15 the melody from
 dB branches
Lead FM electric piano, FM kalimba, or -22 dB leaves, with heavy
 Karplus-Strong pluck per mood reverb
 -24 to -34 atmosphere
Bells FM bell (harmonicity 5.07) high-pass dB
 400 Hz

Ambience filtered noise layers: rain, ocean, wind,
 stream, crickets, fire

 Page 11 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Exact starting patches, the full mix table and the Tone.js rules are in the kit's sound-
design skill. A nice detail for the README: Karplus-Strong synthesis is itself a feedback
loop, so even the pluck sound is recursive.

Ambience and samples

Build ambience procedurally first. It needs no files or licences and renders cleanly in the
offline export. If there is time, add two to four recorded loops from Pixabay, which the
brief itself suggests. Pixabay content is free to use without attribution, but it cannot be
redistributed as standalone files (Pixabay licence); credit it in CREDITS.md anyway. For a
sampled lead, VSCO 2 Community Edition is public domain (CC0) (Versilian Studios).

Research to cite in the README

 A web-based listening study of 293 adults identified the elements that promoted
 relaxation: no accentuation, legato, soft (pp�mp) dynamics, smooth melodic shape,
 repetition, middle register, rubato, thin texture and smooth transitions. Legato, absent
 accents and rubato mattered most (Conrad et al., medRxiv preprint, 2023). The
 composer's rules map onto each of these. The same study found medium tempos (80�
 100 bpm) relaxing, so let users raise the tempo instead of forcing very slow pieces.
 A study that slowed the tempo to 45 bpm, softened the timbre and lowered the
 volume found two distinct responder profiles among listeners (Hern�ndez-Ruiz et al.,
 Psychology of Music, 2020). People relax differently, which is the argument for user-
 chosen moods and tempo.

You are the ears

Claude cannot hear. At every audio checkpoint, listen on headphones and on phone
speakers, then report in these words so Claude can map them to changes:

You hear Claude changes

harsh, tinny lower FM index, low-pass the lead at 3�4 kHz,
 quieter bells

muddy, boomy high-pass pads at 150�180 Hz, drop the bass, cut
 low end from the reverb

busy, anxious fewer notes per second, drop ornaments, longer
 notes

 Page 12 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

You hear Claude changes

boring, samey progression moves every phrase, register changes
 per section

aimless phrase starts and strong beats snap to chord tones

clicks, pops longer attacks, ramp every change

The full 13-row table is in the sound-design skill. Spend 20�30 minutes on the first
listening pass; it is the 25% line.

Visual design, relaxation UX and accessibility

Calm here is a design decision: a dark "Nocturne Garden" look, slow motion, one obvious
action at a time, and WCAG 2.2 AA from the first screen. This section carries 55% of the
score (relaxation & UX, visual design, interaction).

Visual system

Token Value

Background ink navy #0B1020 #121A33 , mood-tinted
 horizon glow; never pure black

Text #EEF1F8 primary, #AAB3C8 secondary (9:1 on the
 background)

Glass panels rgba(12,17,34,0.62) + 16 px blur + hairline
 border; keeps text contrast over a bright tree

Accents one family per mood (peach-gold Dawn, teal-sage
 Rain, aqua Ocean, emerald-firefly Forest, amber
 Temple)

Type Fraunces (display), Manrope (UI), JetBrains Mono
 (code view), self-hosted

 bounce; ambient loops 6�10 s

 Page 13 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Avoid: purple gradients on white, neon cyberpunk, neumorphism, the default shadcn look,
 bouncy animation. I ran the ui-ux-pro-max design skill for this brief; it proposed light
 neumorphism in lavender, which suits wellness landing pages, not an immersive night-
 time instrument, and neumorphism carries high accessibility risk. Use that skill for its UX
 checklists only.

 Signature visuals

 Branches glow from a deep trunk colour to luminous tips, with a soft additive glow
 pass.
 Each branch grows over the length of its own note. The playing branch brightens with
 the note's loudness.
 Leaves open as blossoms when their bell rings, then breathe slowly.
 Up to 80 fireflies drift on a slow noise field; a few spark on each bell.
 Wind sway with a 6�10 s period, stronger toward the tips; a �1% breathing zoom every
 10 s.

 Relaxation features

 First-minute ritual: headphones hint, one Begin tap, drone fades in over 6 s.
 Moods: one tap changes sound, palette and ambience together, with a 3 s crossfade.
 Nothing jumps: parameter changes regenerate after 400 ms and crossfade over 2 s.
 Atmosphere mixer: rain, ocean, wind, stream, crickets, fire.
 Breathing companion: a ring that grows for 4 s and shrinks for 6 s.
 Sleep timer: 15, 30 or 60 minutes, then a 60 s fade.
 Zen mode: hides all UI; any key brings it back.
 Calm copy: "Plant a seed", "Your song is ready", "Keep this song". No exclamation
 marks.
 In-key UI sounds: optional, quantised to the scale and the beat, so interacting never
 breaks the music.

 Interaction

 Layout: full-bleed canvas, floating glass transport bar, a control drawer (right on
 desktop, bottom sheet on mobile) with World, Sound, Atmosphere and Session tabs.
 Every slider has a plain-language explanation of its musical effect, for example
 "Depth: how many times each branch splits. Deeper trees make longer songs."

 Page 14 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 Shortcuts: Space, N, W, L, Z, E, M, arrows, 1�5, ?, Esc. They can be switched off.
 Share links carry the seed and every parameter; a local "garden" keeps up to 24 seeds.
 Errors are gentle: a toast with retry, and a "Replant" recovery screen.

Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

 Full keyboard operation, visible focus that the transport bar never hides, no keyboard
 traps.
 Contrast 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for controls, measured over the brightest part of the
 tree.
 Reduced-motion mode (system setting or in-app switch): no sway, drift or zoom; fades
 only. Nothing flashes more than 3 times a second.
 The canvas has a live text description, such as "A fractal tree, 127 branches, 7 levels
 deep, playing in D major pentatonic at 60 BPM".
 Sliders announce values with units; status changes are announced politely; touch
 targets are at least 24 px (aim for 44).
 Audio never autoplays; pause and volume are always one step away; a mono switch
 helps people with hearing in one ear.
 Automated: axe checks in the end-to-end tests must report zero serious or critical
 issues.

Audio export

Export renders the score offline through the exact instrument rack used for live playback.
The file therefore sounds identical to what the user heard, and it renders faster than real
time. Export is a mandatory deliverable, so it is built before you sleep (Phase 5), not on the
last day.

Format How Priority
WAV, 16-bit (default) or 24- Must
bit Tone.Offline own encoder with dither and Must
MIDI title/seed metadata Should

MP3, 192 kbps @tonejs/midi , one track per voice, so musicians
 can open it in a DAW

 @breezystack/lamejs in a Web Worker (LGPL;
 credit it)

 Page 15 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Format How Priority
Cover art, 1600�1600 PNG Should
Live session recording snapshot of the finished tree with title, mood and Should
Video seed Could

 Tone.Recorder : WebM/Opus or MP4/AAC
 depending on the browser

 canvas stream + audio through MediaRecorder

Pipeline

 1. Build the rack inside Tone.Offline with the same createRack() used live.
 2. Await the reverb's ready promise (and any samples) before starting the transport.

 Skipping this is the classic cause of silent or dry exports.
 3. Render the score plus an 8-second tail, fade the last 3 seconds, and peak-normalise to

 -1 dBFS.
 4. Encode, with progress (rendering encoding done) and a cancel button.
 5. Name the file seedsong_<mood>_<seed>_<date>.wav and write the share link into its

 metadata, so every file can be regrown.

Proof it works: an end-to-end test downloads a WAV and checks that it is over 200 KB
with RMS above -45 dBFS. npm run audio:qa renders every mood and fails on clipping,
wrong loudness or long silences.

 Page 16 of 40
 Recursive Soundscapes -- Winning Build Plan (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

 24-hour timeline

 Build timeline � Wed 25 23:20 to Thu 26 22:00, GMT+6

 The night builds the engine, so the riskiest technical parts (composer, audio, export) are
 done while you are fresh. The morning goes to what judges feel (visuals, relaxation UX).
 The afternoon makes recursion visible, adds a world, and hardens accessibility and
 performance. Nothing new starts after 18:30.

 Checkpoint 04:30: a full piece plays and exports. If not, skip the overnight goal and fix
 export first; it is mandatory.
 Checkpoint 13:30: the app shell, moods and tools work on the live URL. If you are
 behind, run the behind-schedule prompt and cut Hanoi, video export and PWA.
 Checkpoint 18:30: feature freeze. Only fixes, docs and the demo video after this.
 12:00: the submission link is released. Open it straight away so there are no surprises
 at 21:00.

# Seedsong: Recursive Soundscapes (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Solo 24-hour hackathon build. Hard deadline: **Thu 26 Nov 2026, 22:00 GMT+6**. Feature freeze: **18:30 GMT+6**.
Seedsong is a browser app where a recursive function grows a glowing fractal tree and the call tree itself becomes relaxing music.
The full product and technical spec is `docs/SPEC.md`. Read the section a task names before you start it. The official rubric and what a 10/10 looks like are in `docs/RUBRIC.md`.

## How we are judged (optimise in this order)

| Weight | Criterion | What it means for every decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 35% | Relaxation & UX | a calm first minute, no harsh sound or motion, frictionless controls, mobile works |
| 25% | Musical quality | notes locked to the scale, voice-led chords, soft timbres, a real mix (limiter, about -16 to -18 LUFS), real musical form |
| 15% | Creative use of recursion | the call tree IS the musical form; recursion is visible (lens, code view, skyline) and audible (Wander/Bloom) |
| 10% | Visual design | bioluminescent tree, one coherent token system, 60 fps |
| 10% | Interaction & usability | moods, clear labels, keyboard shortcuts, share links |
| 5% | Technical execution | tests, CI, deploy, reliable export, clean architecture |

Mandatory deliverables (all must work in the deployed build): configurable recursion, interactive visualization, procedural music from the recursion, UI controls + playback, audio export, and a polished, accessible, relaxing experience.

## Stack (ask before changing)

Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript 7 (strict) · Tone.js 15 · Canvas 2D · Tailwind CSS 4 + CSS variables · Radix UI primitives · Zustand · Motion · Lucide icons · Fontsource fonts (Fraunces, Manrope, JetBrains Mono) · Vitest 5 + Testing Library · Playwright + @axe-core/playwright · oxlint + Prettier · GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages.

- Keep the create-vite defaults (oxlint, TypeScript 7). Do NOT add ESLint or typescript-eslint; typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7 yet.
- Tone.js v15: use `getTransport()`, `getDestination()`, `getDraw()`, `getContext()`. Never use the deprecated `Tone.Transport`, `Tone.Destination`, `Tone.Draw` or `Tone.context`.
- Unsure about a library API? Check Context7 (MCP) or the typings in `node_modules`. Never guess an API.
- Verify package versions with `npm view <pkg> version` before adding them.

## Commands

- `npm run dev` / `npm run build` / `npm run preview`
- `npm run verify`: typecheck + lint + unit tests + build. It must pass before every commit.
- `npm run test` (Vitest) · `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright: smoke, export, a11y)
- `npm run audio:qa`: renders reference seeds offline and checks peak, loudness and silence
- `npm run logs:collect`: copies every Claude Code transcript for this repo into `ai-logs/`

## Architecture rules

- One source of truth: `RecursionTrace` (pure) → `Score` (pure) → { live playback, offline export, MIDI, visuals }. Visuals and export never re-derive music.
- `src/core/**` is pure TypeScript: no DOM, no Tone.js, no React. It is deterministic for a given (params, seed) and fully unit-tested.
- `src/audio/**` owns Tone.js. ONE rack factory, `createRack(context, mood)`, serves BOTH live playback and `Tone.Offline` export.
- `src/viz/**` owns canvas rendering. It never schedules audio; it reacts to note events the scheduler emits through `getDraw()`.
- `src/ui/**` holds React components; state lives in `src/state` (Zustand). No business logic in components.
- Randomness only from the seeded PRNG in `src/core/random.ts`. `Math.random` is banned outside tests.
- New recursion worlds plug in through the `WorldDefinition` interface. Never special-case a world in audio or export code.

## Definition of done (every task)

1. `npm run verify` passes, and new logic has tests.
2. UI change: open the app with the Playwright MCP, take screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844, fix what looks off, and confirm zero console errors.
3. Audio change: tell the user exactly what to listen for. They are the ears; you cannot hear.
4. Accessibility: keyboard reachable, visible focus, real labels, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, nothing flashes more than 3 times a second.
5. Commit in small steps with conventional messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`).
6. End every turn with: what changed · how to see or hear it · known issues · the next step.

## Relaxation rules (never break)

- No sudden loud sounds. Every start, stop and change ramps: at least 50 ms against clicks, 1–3 s for scene changes. Master limiter at -1 dBTP.
- Notes are always quantised to the active scale. Default tempo 48–64 BPM. At most about 4 notes per second.
- Motion is slow: ambient loops last 6 s or longer, UI transitions 200–400 ms, no bounce, no shake, no flashing.
- Copy is short, warm and in the second person. No exclamation marks and no emoji in the UI.

## Scope discipline

Follow the MoSCoW list in `docs/SPEC.md` §3. Never start a Could before every Must is done and verified. Ask before adding a dependency that is not listed above. After 18:30 GMT+6 only fixes, docs and polish.

## AI logging (missing logs can disqualify us)

Hooks in `.claude/settings.json` log every prompt and response to `ai-logs/`. Never delete, rewrite or move anything in `ai-logs/`, and never disable or edit the hooks. If `ai-logs/.hook-errors.log` gains entries, tell the user immediately.

## Project skills and agents

- Skills: `verify` (runs before every commit), `sound-design` (music theory, Tone.js recipes, mixing), `calm-ux` (relaxation UX, motion, WCAG 2.2 AA), `/judge` (rubric review in a forked agent).
- Agents for independent review: `rubric-judge`, `a11y-auditor`, `music-director`. Use them after each major phase; do not grade your own work.

# Seedsong: Product and Technical Specification Version 1.0 · 25 Nov 2026 · Hub's Quest Epoch 1 "Recursive Soundscapes" > Make recursion audible. Make simulation beautiful. Make the experience relaxing. (from the brief) --- ## §0 Vision and principles Seedsong turns one recursive function into a garden you listen to. The user plants a seed (a set of recursion parameters), watches a luminous fractal tree grow, and hears the call tree become a calm piece of music. When it finishes they keep the song. Principles, in priority order: 1. **Calm before clever.** Every feature must lower stress. If something can startle, it is wrong. 2. **Beautiful by default.** The first click, with zero configuration, must sound and look finished. 3. **The structure is the music.** Musical form comes from the shape of the recursion, not from decoration on top of it. 4. **Show the mathematics.** Anyone can see which call is playing and why it sounds the way it does. 5. **One source of truth.** Trace → Score → (audio, export, MIDI, visuals). Nothing drifts out of sync. ## §1 Experience ### §1.1 The first minute (what judges see first) 1. **Landing.** Deep night gradient, slow drifting motes, the title *Seedsong* in Fraunces, and one seed glyph pulsing at breathing pace (10 s cycle, about 6 breaths a minute). A line reads "Best with headphones". One primary button: **Begin**. The click unlocks audio, which browsers require anyway. 2. **0–8 s.** A warm drone fades in over 6 s. The trunk grows upward with a low note. 3. **8–60 s.** Boughs split into harmony, branches carry the melody, twigs sparkle, and leaves open as glowing blossoms with bell tones. The recursion lens shows the current call. 4. **End.** The recursion unwinds, the music resolves to the home chord, the tree sways gently, and the **Keep this song** button glows softly. ### §1.2 Core loop Choose a mood → shape the seed → grow and listen → keep (export, share link, save to garden). Moods are one-tap presets; parameters are for exploring. ### §1.3 Personas - **The tired student** wants ten calm minutes. Uses a mood, zen mode and the sleep timer. Never opens the parameter drawer. - **The curious coder** wants to see recursion. Opens the recursion lens and code view, toggles Wander/Bloom, changes depth. - **The musician** wants material. Exports WAV and MIDI and shares seeds. ## §2 Rubric mapping | Criterion (weight) | Features that earn it | | --- | --- | | Relaxation & UX (35%) | first-minute ritual, moods, crossfades, ambience mixer, breathing companion, sleep timer, zen mode, calm copy, mobile layout, no harsh peaks | | Musical quality (25%) | scale lock, fractal form with chord progression and cadences, voice-leading, five designed moods, mix chain, density cap, audio QA | | Creative recursion (15%) | fractal-form mapping, recursion lens, code view, depth skyline, Wander vs Bloom, extra worlds (L-system, Hanoi) | | Visual design (10%) | design tokens, bioluminescent rendering, growth synced to notes, particles, palettes per mood | | Interaction & usability (10%) | plain-language controls, presets, keyboard shortcuts, share links, garden, onboarding, help | | Technical execution (5%) | pure tested core, single rack for live and offline, CI/CD, deployed demo, export tests, performance budgets | ## §3 Scope (MoSCoW) **Must (ship by 04:00 for skeleton, all verified by 15:00):** - M1 Fractal Grove world with configurable depth, branching, spread, length ratio, randomness, asymmetry, seed (§4.1) - M2 Composer with fractal form, Wander mode, scale lock, cadences, density cap (§5) - M3 Live audio engine: five moods, pad/lead/bell/drone voices, reverb/delay, master limiter, procedural ambience (§6) - M4 Canvas visualizer with growth synced to notes, glow, particles, sway, reduced motion (§7) - M5 Transport: play, pause, stop, seek, volume, regenerate with crossfade (§8) - M6 Export: offline-rendered WAV (16-bit) with progress, plus MIDI (§9) - M7 Landing ritual, moods, control drawer, mobile layout, keyboard access, WCAG 2.2 AA basics (§8) - C4 PWA install + offline, Media Session lock-screen controls - C5 Video export (canvas + audio via MediaRecorder) - C6 Bangla UI language toggle **Won't (this time):** accounts, backend, database, social feed, AI-generated music, payments. --- ## §4 Recursion worlds ### §4.0 Shared model ```ts type WorldId = 'grove' | 'lsystem' | 'hanoi'; interface ParamSpec { key: string; label: string; help: string; // help = one plain-language sentence min: number; max: number; step: number; default: number; unit?: string; format?: (v: number) => string; // value text for aria-valuetext } interface TraceNode { id: number; parentId: number | null; depth: number; childIndex: number; siblingCount: number; isLeaf: boolean; params: Record; // e.g. { length, angle } geom: { x1: number; y1: number; x2: number; y2: number; width: number }; order: { call: number; ret: number }; // DFS indices of call and return events } interface RecursionTrace { worldId: WorldId; seed: string; params: Record; nodes: TraceNode[]; // in call order events: Array<{ kind: 'call' | 'return'; nodeId: number }>; maxDepth: number; truncated: boolean; bounds: { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number }; } interface WorldDefinition

{ id: WorldId; name: string; tagline: string; params: ParamSpec[]; defaults: P; generate(params: P, rng: Rng): RecursionTrace; // pure codeSnippet: string; // shown in code view, 10–14 lines lineFor(event: 'call' | 'base' | 'return'): number; // line to highlight in code view } ``` Randomness: `cyrb128(seedString)` → `sfc32` PRNG. Seeds are human-friendly words (`still-lake-07`), generated from a small calm word list. ### §4.1 World 1: Fractal Grove (hero, Must) ```ts function branch(x, y, angle, length, depth) { emitCall(node) // a note begins if (depth < maxDepth && length > minLength) { // recursive case for (let i = 0; i < branching; i++) { const offset = branching === 1 ? 0 : spread * (2 * i / (branching - 1) - 1) const jitter = (rng() - 0.5) * 2 * randomness * spread * 0.6 const lean = asymmetry * spread * 0.5 const next = length * ratio * (1 + (rng() - 0.5) * randomness * 0.4) branch(x2, y2, angle + offset + jitter + lean, next, depth + 1) } } // base case: a leaf (bell) emitReturn(node) // the phrase resolves } ``` | Param | Range | Default | Help text | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | depth | 1–10 (clamped by branching) | 7 | How many times each branch splits. Deeper trees make longer songs. | | branching | 2–4 | 2 | How many new branches grow from each tip. More branches, richer harmony. | | spread | 5–60° | 24° | How wide the branches open. Wider trees sound more spacious. | | ratio | 0.55–0.82 | 0.72 | How much shorter each branch is than its parent. Shorter branches make quicker notes. | | randomness | 0–1 | 0.25 | How much the wind bends each branch. Adds gentle variation. | | asymmetry | -1–1 | 0 | Leans the tree left or right. Shifts the melody up or down. | | seed | text | random words | Same seed, same song. Share it with a friend. | Depth clamp so the full tree fits a 2,047-node budget: branching 2 → max depth 10; 3 → 6; 4 → 5. The depth slider max follows the branching value. Never truncate a tree halfway (lopsided trees sound broken). ### §4.2 World 2: L-System Garden (Should) - Recursive expansion, not string replacement: `expand(symbol, depth)` returns the symbol when `depth === 0` or no rule exists; otherwise it calls `expand` for every symbol in the rule. The expand call stack is the recursion trace (call depth = rewrite depth). - Turtle: `F` draws a segment (one node), `+`/`-` rotate, `[` pushes state (a branch begins), `]` pops (the branch returns). - Presets (axiom, rules, angle, iterations): Fern `X` · `X→F+[[X]-X]-F[-FX]+X`, `F→FF` · 25° · 5; Bush `F` · `F→FF+[+F-F-F]-[-F+F+F]` · 22.5° · 4; Koch snowflake `F++F++F` · `F→F-F++F-F` · 60° · 4; Dragon `FX` · `X→X+YF+`, `Y→-FX-Y` · 90° · 10; Sierpinski arrowhead `A` · `A→B-A-B`, `B→A+B+A` · 60° · 6; Hilbert `A` · `A→+BF-AFA-FB+`, `B→-AF+BFB+FA-` · 90° · 5. - Rule editor: validate symbols, balanced brackets, and a 4,000-segment cap (the iteration slider max adapts per preset). ### §4.3 World 3: Hanoi Music Box (Could) - `hanoi(n, from, to, via)`: if `n === 0` return; `hanoi(n-1, from, via, to)`; `move(n, from, to)`; `hanoi(n-1, via, to, from)`. - Discs 3–8 (default 5 → 31 moves). Discs glide on arcs (700 ms, ease-in-out); a soft ripple on landing. - The smallest disc moves every other step, so its notes form a natural ostinato. The move sequence is a fractal rhythm (the ruler sequence). ### §4.4 Making recursion visible (Should) - Recursion lens: live call stack as indented frames, e.g. `branch(depth 3, len 0.37, θ 102°)`, plus counters (calls, current depth, max depth). - Code view: the world's `codeSnippet` with the executing line highlighted. Call → note, base case → bell, return → resolution. - Depth skyline: a stepped silhouette of call depth over time under the transport bar, with playhead and click/keyboard seek. --- ## §5 Composer (trace → score) ### §5.1 Score model ```ts type Voice = 'drone' | 'pad' | 'lead' | 'ornament' | 'bell' | 'bass'; interface ScoreNote { id: string; time: number; duration: number; midi: number; velocity: number; pan: number; voice: Voice; nodeId: number; depth: number } interface ScoreChord { time: number; duration: number; midis: number[]; symbol: string } interface ScoreEvent { time: number; kind: 'call' | 'return' | 'cadence' | 'section'; nodeId: number; depth: number } interface Score { version: 1; seed: string; worldId: WorldId; moodId: MoodId; mode: 'wander' | 'bloom'; bpm: number; key: string; scale: ScaleId; duration: number; tail: number; // seconds notes: ScoreNote[]; chords: ScoreChord[]; events: ScoreEvent[]; stats: { noteCount: number; nodeCount: number; maxDepth: number }; } ``` Times are in seconds from 0. Velocity is 0–1. Pan is -1 to 1. The composer is pure and deterministic. ### §5.2 Scales (semitones from the root) majorPentatonic `[0,2,4,7,9]` · minorPentatonic `[0,3,5,7,10]` · yo `[0,2,5,7,9]` · lydian `[0,2,4,6,7,9,11]` · dorian `[0,2,3,5,7,9,10]` · aeolian `[0,2,3,5,7,8,10]` · ionian `[0,2,4,5,7,9,11]`. Melody arithmetic happens in scale degrees (an index into the scale across octaves), so every note is in the scale by construction. ### §5.3 Fractal form (the core idea) | Recursion level | Musical role | Voice | | --- | --- | --- | | Trunk (depth 0) | the key; a root + fifth drone for the whole piece | drone | | Boughs (depth 1) | sections A, B (C, D) of the piece | section events, pad colour | | Depth 2 | phrases; each depth-2 subtree is one phrase with one chord from the mood's progression (cycled) | pad | | Depth 3 to maxDepth-2 | the melody | lead | | Twigs (maxDepth-1) | ornaments: quieter, higher, thinned by density | ornament | | Leaves (base case) | bells: chord tones, upper octave, long ring | bell | | Return from a depth-2 call | cadence: soft pad re-swell + one beat of rest | pad | | Return from the root | final cadence to the tonic + 8–12 s tail | pad, drone | For shallow trees (maxDepth ≤ 3) the melody starts at depth 1. The last phrase always ends on the tonic chord. ### §5.4 Wander (depth-first, default) - Walk the trace events in order. A `call` at depth ≥ 3 emits a lead note; twigs emit ornaments; leaves emit bells. - Beat = 60 / bpm seconds. Lead duration in beats = quantise(lerp(0.5, 2, sqrt(length / trunkLength))) to {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2}. Ornaments 0.5 beat. Bells ring 4 beats but advance the cursor only 0.5 beat. - Pitch: degree(child) = degree(parent) + step. For branching 2, left child +0 and right child +2 (a gentle climb toward the leaves); for 3–4 children, steps spread across -1…+2. Branch jitter adds ±1 degree with probability = randomness × 0.5 (seeded). - At a phrase start, snap to the nearest chord tone. On strong beats (1 and 3 of 4/4), move non-chord tones to the nearest chord tone. - Lead range MIDI 60–84 (reflect at the edges). Never repeat one pitch more than 3 times in a row. - Bells: the chord tone nearest to lead + 12, clamped to MIDI 72–96. ### §5.5 Bloom (breadth-first, Should) - Level 0 starts the drone; level 1 swells the first chord; each level d ≥ 2 becomes a 2-bar phrase. - Nodes in a level are sorted by x (left → right, like a harp sweep) and spread across the phrase with seeded offsets of ±0.15 beat. - Pitches come from the current chord; register rises one step per level. The chord progression advances once per level. - Cap 12 notes per phrase. Pick a seeded, evenly spaced subset when a level is larger. End with a return to the tonic. ### §5.6 Dynamics, density, humanisation, length - Velocity = clamp(0.62 × 0.92^depth × form(t) × (1 ± 0.08 seeded), 0.12, 0.85). `form(t)` rises 0.7 → 1.0 over the first 25% of the piece, holds to 70%, and falls to 0.75 at the end. - Density cap: at most `mood.maxNotesPerSecond` (default 3.5) in any 1 s window. Drop lowest priority first: ornaments, then bells, then lead (never drone or pad). - Humanise onsets ±12 ms (lead), ±20 ms (bells). Never below 0. - Target length 90 s–6 min. If longer, raise tempo up to +15% then thin the deepest level. If shorter, slow down to the mood's minimum tempo. ### §5.7 Mappings for other worlds - L-System: each `F` is a note; `+`/`-` move one scale degree up/down; `[` saves pitch and starts a quieter harmony voice one register up; `]` restores the saved pitch (melodic return). Bracket depth lowers velocity by 8% per level. Rewrite depth chooses the voice (shallow = lead, deep = ornament). - Hanoi: disc n → degree (N − n) (larger discs lower); peg → pan (-0.6, 0, 0.6) and voice (pluck, lead, bell); one move per beat; call depth → velocity. ### §5.8 Endless Drift (Could) After a piece ends, generate the next seed, modulate to the key a fifth up (circle of fifths), and crossfade over 8 s. --- ## §6 Sound design ### §6.1 Moods | Mood | Root, scale | BPM | Progression (pad) | Lead | Ambience | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Dawn Mist | D, majorPentatonic (harmony from D major) | 60 | Dadd9 – Bm7 – Gmaj7 – Asus4 → D | soft FM electric piano | birds + breeze | | Rain Garden | A, minorPentatonic (harmony from A aeolian) | 56 | Am(add9) – Fmaj7 – C – G → Am | FM kalimba pluck | rain | | Deep Ocean | C, lydian | 50 | Cmaj7 – D/C – Em7 – Cmaj7(#11) | sparse glass bells + pad swells | ocean waves | | Night Forest | F♯, minorPentatonic | 54 | F♯m – D – A – Esus2 → F♯m | harp-like Karplus–Strong pluck | crickets + stream | | Temple | D, yo | 48 | open fifths and fourths over a D drone (no functional progression) | koto-like pluck | wind + distant chimes | In Deep Ocean the F♯ (Lydian 4th) may only appear as a short note on a weak beat. ### §6.2 Voices (Tone.js v15 starting patches; tune by ear) - **Pad:** `PolySynth(Synth, { oscillator: { type: 'fattriangle', count: 3, spread: 18 }, envelope: { attack: 2.5, decay: 1, sustain: 0.8, release: 6 } })` → `Filter(1200, 'lowpass', -24)` with a 0.05 Hz LFO (700–1600 Hz) → `Chorus(0.3, 3.5, 0.4).start()`. -18 dB. - **Electric piano lead:** `PolySynth(FMSynth, { harmonicity: 3, modulationIndex: 2.5, envelope: { attack: 0.01, decay: 1.6, sustain: 0.15, release: 2.4 }, modulationEnvelope: { attack: 0.01, decay: 0.6, sustain: 0.1, release: 1.2 } })`. -14 dB. - **Kalimba:** `PolySynth(FMSynth, { harmonicity: 8, modulationIndex: 2, envelope: { attack: 0.001, decay: 0.9, sustain: 0, release: 1.2 } })`. -15 dB. - **Pluck (harp/koto):** `PluckSynth({ attackNoise: 0.6, dampening: 3000, resonance: 0.92 })` (Karplus–Strong: a feedback delay line, a recursion in sound). -12 dB. - **Bells:** `PolySynth(FMSynth, { harmonicity: 5.07, modulationIndex: 9, envelope: { attack: 0.002, decay: 3.5, sustain: 0, release: 3 } })` → `Filter(400, 'highpass')`. -22 dB, heavy reverb send. - **Drone:** two detuned sines (root, fifth) with a 6 s attack and slow amplitude LFO (0.07 Hz, depth 0.15). -24 dB. - **Bass (optional):** `MonoSynth` sine, attack 1.2 s, release 4 s, on chord roots. -20 dB. - Set `maxPolyphony` to 16 per PolySynth. ### §6.3 Effects and master - Sends: `Reverb({ decay: 9, preDelay: 0.04 })` (await `ready`), `FeedbackDelay('4n.', 0.3)` at wet 0.2 on lead and bells. - Master: `EQ3({ low: 0, mid: -1, high: -3 })` → `Compressor({ threshold: -20, ratio: 2.5, attack: 0.03, release: 0.3 })` → `Limiter(-1)` → destination. - Targets: peak ≤ -1 dBFS, integrated loudness about -18 to -16 LUFS, warm spectrum (gentle high-shelf cut). - Optional mono switch (`Tone.Mono`) for single-sided hearing. ### §6.4 Ambience Procedural layers first (no files, no licences, work offline): - Rain: pink noise → band 400–3,500 Hz, -28 dB, plus random droplet blips (short filtered noise, seeded timing). - Ocean: brown noise → `AutoFilter(0.08 Hz, base 200 Hz, 3 octaves)` + slow tremolo (12 s waves). -24 dB. - Wind: pink noise → slow-sweeping band-pass. -30 dB. - Stream: white noise → band-pass 1.5–3 kHz with fast random modulation. -32 dB. - Crickets: quiet high FM chirps at seeded random intervals. -34 dB. - Fire: brown noise + random crackles. -30 dB. Optional recorded loops (Should, if time): 2–4 seamless loops from pixabay.com (free, no attribution required; credit them anyway in CREDITS.md), 64–96 kbps OGG/MP3, 30–60 s, in `public/audio/ambience/`. Optional sampled lead: VSCO 2 Community Edition or VCSL (both CC0), a few notes per instrument, used with `Tone.Sampler`. ### §6.5 UI sounds Off by default. When on: a soft sine blip quantised to the current scale and the next 8th note, -30 dB, on primary actions only. --- ## §7 Visual design ### §7.1 Tokens ("Nocturne Garden") - Background: `--bg-0 #0B1020` (ink navy), `--bg-1 #121A33`, mood horizon glow as a radial gradient. Never pure black. - Text: `--text-1 #EEF1F8`, `--text-2 #AAB3C8` (9:1 on bg-0). Body 16 px, line-height 1.5. - Glass surfaces: `rgba(12,17,34,0.62)` + `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)` + 1 px border `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)`, radius 16 px. Keep text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 even over a bright glow. - Mood accents: Dawn `#F5B38A` / `#F28FB0` / `#FFD98A` · Rain `#7FD1C7` / `#A8C5A0` · Ocean `#6FD6F0` / `#8FB8FF` · Night Forest `#7EE0A1` / `#F4E27A` · Temple `#F2B45A` / `#E8875B`. One accent family per mood. - Type: Fraunces (display; soft, organic), Manrope (UI), JetBrains Mono (recursion lens, code view). Self-hosted via Fontsource. Scale 12/14/16/20/28/40/64. - Motion: micro 200 ms, panels 400 ms, scenes 1,200–2,000 ms; enter `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, crossfade `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`. No bounce. - Icons: Lucide, 1.5 px stroke. No emoji. Focus ring 2 px accent + 2 px offset. - Avoid: purple-on-white gradients, neon cyberpunk, neumorphism, glassmorphism without a contrast backstop, default shadcn look. ### §7.2 Rendering - Canvas 2D, devicePixelRatio scaling, layers: sky (gradient, a few slow-twinkling stars, horizon glow, ground mist), tree, glow, particles. Vignette + very faint static grain (≤ 3% opacity). - Branch width = trunkWidth × ratio^depth (trunk 10–14 px → tips 0.75 px), round caps. Colour runs from the mood's deep tone at the trunk to the luminous accent at the tips; a second wide, low-alpha pass with `'lighter'` compositing adds glow. - Growth: each branch draws over its note's duration (easeOutCubic). The playing branch brightens with velocity and fades over the release time. - Leaves: blossoms (radial-gradient petals) scale in on their bell note, then breathe (opacity 0.7–1.0, 6–10 s, phase-offset). - Particles: ≤ 80 fireflies/pollen on a slow noise field (< 20 px/s); small bursts of 3–6 on bell notes. - Wind sway: per-branch rotation `sin(t·ω + depth·φ) × amp × depth / maxDepth`, period 6–10 s; children follow parents. - Camera: fit tree bounds with padding; breathing zoom ±1% over 10 s. - Batch strokes per depth level (one path per level) to stay at 60 fps with 2,000 branches. Pause rendering when the tab is hidden. - Reduced motion: no sway, no drift, no zoom; fades only. Nothing may flash more than 3 times per second. - Sync: visuals react to events the scheduler emits via `getDraw().schedule()`; never `setTimeout` for audio-visual sync. --- ## §8 UX and accessibility ### §8.1 Layout - Full-bleed canvas. Top bar: logo (a tiny recursive Y-branch glyph) left; help, zen, fullscreen right. - Floating glass transport bar (bottom centre, max 720 px): play/pause, new seed, Wander/Bloom, time + depth skyline, volume, Keep (export). - Control drawer: right side 360 px on desktop, bottom sheet on mobile. Tabs: **World** (world picker + params), **Sound** (mood, key, scale, tempo, instrument mix), **Atmosphere** (ambience mixer, reverb space), **Session** (breathing, sleep timer, mono, reduce motion, UI sounds, shortcuts on/off). - Mood chips: five chips above the transport bar; selecting one crossfades sound, palette and ambience over 3 s. ### §8.2 Interaction - Recursion param changes regenerate after a 400 ms debounce and crossfade over 2 s. Sound params apply live with ramps. - Shortcuts (can be turned off; never fire inside inputs): Space play/pause · N new seed · W Wander/Bloom · L lens · Z zen · E export · M mute · ←/→ seek 10 s · ↑/↓ volume · 1–5 moods · ? help · Esc close. - Zen mode hides all UI (cursor hides after 3 s idle); any key or click shows it again. - Breathing companion: ring that grows 4 s (inhale) and shrinks 6 s (exhale), optional, aligned to phrase starts when possible. - Sleep timer: 15/30/60 min with a 60 s fade-out, then pause. - Share link: params, world, mood, mode and seed in the URL hash. Garden: up to 24 saved seeds in localStorage with thumbnail, rename, delete. - Onboarding: 3 short cards on first visit (plant a seed · watch it grow · keep your song), skippable, remembered. - Toasts: polite, auto-dismiss after 4 s, also announced via `aria-live="polite"`. - Errors: AudioContext unavailable → calm explanation; export failure → toast with retry; an error boundary with a **Replant** button. Params persist to localStorage. ### §8.3 Copy tone Short, warm, second person, no exclamation marks, no emoji, no jargon outside the lens and code view. Examples: "Plant a seed", "Your song is ready", "Breathe in", "Keep this song". ### §8.4 Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) - Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 text, ≥ 3:1 UI components and focus indicators (1.4.3, 1.4.11). - Full keyboard operation, logical focus order, visible focus not hidden by the sticky transport bar (2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11). - Character-key shortcuts can be turned off (2.1.4). - Targets ≥ 24×24 CSS px; aim for 44×44 (2.5.8). Every slider also works with keys and click (2.5.7). - Moving content can be paused: zen visuals pause with playback; reduce-motion switch (2.2.2). - No more than 3 flashes per second (2.3.1). - Audio never autoplays; volume and pause are always reachable (1.4.2). - Canvas has `role="img"` and a live description, e.g. "A fractal tree, 127 branches, 7 levels deep, playing in D major pentatonic at 60 BPM" (1.1.1). - Sliders use `aria-valuetext` with units. State changes are announced politely (4.1.3). - `lang="en"`, responsive to 320 px width, zoom to 200% without loss (1.4.4, 1.4.10). --- ## §9 Export - **WAV (Must):** `renderScore()` via `Tone.Offline` using the same `createRack()`; await reverb (and any sample) readiness inside the callback. 44.1 kHz stereo. 16-bit with TPDF dither (default) or 24-bit. Optional peak normalise to -1 dBFS (default on), 3 s fade-out, tail 8 s (adjustable 0–20 s), ambience included (toggle). - **MIDI (Must):** `@tonejs/midi`, one track per voice, tempo and track names. - **MP3 (Should):** `@breezystack/lamejs` (LGPL; credit it) at 192 kbps in a Web Worker with progress. - **Cover art (Should):** 1600×1600 PNG of the finished tree with title, mood and seed. - **Live session recording (Should):** `Tone.Recorder` (WebM/Opus or MP4/AAC depending on the browser); captures live tweaks and ambience. - **Video (Could):** canvas `captureStream(30)` + audio via `MediaStreamDestination` → `MediaRecorder`. - Progress: rendering → encoding → done, with cancel. Report offline progress by suspending the context at intervals where supported; otherwise show an estimate. - Filename: `seedsong___.`. - WAV metadata (LIST/INFO): INAM title, IART "Seedsong", ICMT share URL, ISFT "Seedsong 1.0 (Tone.js)", ICRD date. ## §10 Architecture ``` src/ app/ App.tsx, providers, ErrorBoundary core/ random.ts, url.ts (share codec) worlds/ types.ts, grove.ts, lsystem.ts, hanoi.ts, registry.ts music/ theory.ts, moods.ts, compose.ts, wander.ts, bloom.ts, density.ts audio/ engine.ts, rack.ts, scheduler.ts, bus.ts, ios.ts instruments/ pad.ts, keys.ts, kalimba.ts, pluck.ts, bells.ts, drone.ts, bass.ts ambience/ rain.ts, ocean.ts, wind.ts, stream.ts, crickets.ts, fire.ts export/ offline.ts, wav.ts, mp3.worker.ts, midi.ts, cover.ts, record.ts, download.ts viz/ renderer.ts, grove-renderer.ts, lsystem-renderer.ts, hanoi-renderer.ts, particles.ts, sky.ts, camera.ts, palette.ts ui/ components/ (TransportBar, ControlDrawer, MoodChips, ParamSlider, RecursionLens, CodeView, DepthSkyline, ExportDialog, Onboarding, HelpOverlay, Toasts …), hooks/ state/ store.ts (Zustand slices: session, params, audio, ui, garden) styles/ tokens.css, global.css workers/ compose.worker.ts (generate + compose off the main thread) tests/e2e/ smoke.spec.ts, export.spec.ts, a11y.spec.ts, keyboard.spec.ts scripts/ audio-qa.mjs, render-samples.mjs, collect-ai-logs.mjs ``` - AudioEngine API: `unlock()`, `load(score, mood)`, `play()`, `pause()`, `stop()`, `seek(s)`, `setVolume(v)`, `setAmbience(layer, v)`, `setMono(on)`, `crossfadeTo(score, mood)`, `dispose()`. - iOS: on unlock set `navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback'` when supported (plays even with the silent switch on); otherwise fall back to a looping silent `

# Seedsong: Product and Technical Specification Version 1.0 · 25 Nov 2026 · Hub's Quest Epoch 1 "Recursive Soundscapes" > Make recursion audible. Make simulation beautiful. Make the experience relaxing. (from the brief) --- ## §0 Vision and principles Seedsong turns one recursive function into a garden you listen to. The user plants a seed (a set of recursion parameters), watches a luminous fractal tree grow, and hears the call tree become a calm piece of music. When it finishes they keep the song. Principles, in priority order: 1. **Calm before clever.** Every feature must lower stress. If something can startle, it is wrong. 2. **Beautiful by default.** The first click, with zero configuration, must sound and look finished. 3. **The structure is the music.** Musical form comes from the shape of the recursion, not from decoration on top of it. 4. **Show the mathematics.** Anyone can see which call is playing and why it sounds the way it does. 5. **One source of truth.** Trace → Score → (audio, export, MIDI, visuals). Nothing drifts out of sync. ## §1 Experience ### §1.1 The first minute (what judges see first) 1. **Landing.** Deep night gradient, slow drifting motes, the title *Seedsong* in Fraunces, and one seed glyph pulsing at breathing pace (10 s cycle, about 6 breaths a minute). A line reads "Best with headphones". One primary button: **Begin**. The click unlocks audio, which browsers require anyway. 2. **0–8 s.** A warm drone fades in over 6 s. The trunk grows upward with a low note. 3. **8–60 s.** Boughs split into harmony, branches carry the melody, twigs sparkle, and leaves open as glowing blossoms with bell tones. The recursion lens shows the current call. 4. **End.** The recursion unwinds, the music resolves to the home chord, the tree sways gently, and the **Keep this song** button glows softly. ### §1.2 Core loop Choose a mood → shape the seed → grow and listen → keep (export, share link, save to garden). Moods are one-tap presets; parameters are for exploring. ### §1.3 Personas - **The tired student** wants ten calm minutes. Uses a mood, zen mode and the sleep timer. Never opens the parameter drawer. - **The curious coder** wants to see recursion. Opens the recursion lens and code view, toggles Wander/Bloom, changes depth. - **The musician** wants material. C4 PWA install + offline, Media Session lock-screen controls - C5 Video export (canvas + audio via MediaRecorder) - C6 Bangla UI language toggle **Won't (this time):** accounts, backend, database, social feed, AI-generated music, payments. --- ## §4 Recursion worlds ### §4.0 Shared model ```ts type WorldId = 'grove' | 'lsystem' | 'hanoi'; interface ParamSpec { key: string; label: string; help: string; // help = one plain-language sentence min: number; max: number; step: number; default: number; unit?: string; format?: (v: number) => string; // value text for aria-valuetext } interface TraceNode { id: number; parentId: number | null; depth: number; childIndex: number; siblingCount: number; isLeaf: boolean; params: Record; // e.g. { length, angle } geom: { x1: number; y1: number; x2: number; y2: number; width: number }; order: { call: number; ret: number }; // DFS indices of call and return events } interface RecursionTrace { worldId: WorldId; seed: string; params: Record; nodes: TraceNode[]; // in call order events: Array<{ kind: 'call' | 'return'; nodeId: number }>; maxDepth: number; truncated: boolean; bounds: { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number }; } interface WorldDefinition

{ id: WorldId; name: string; tagline: string; params: ParamSpec[]; defaults: P; generate(params: P, rng: Rng): RecursionTrace; // pure codeSnippet: string; // shown in code view, 10–14 lines lineFor(event: 'call' | 'base' | 'return'): number; // line to highlight in code view } ``` Randomness: `cyrb128(seedString)` → `sfc32` PRNG. Seeds are human-friendly words (`still-lake-07`), generated from a small calm word list. ### §4.1 World 1: Fractal Grove (hero, Must) ```ts function branch(x, y, angle, length, depth) { emitCall(node) // a note begins if (depth < maxDepth && length > minLength) { // recursive case for (let i = 0; i < branching; i++) { const offset = branching === 1 ? 0 : spread * (2 * i / (branching - 1) - 1) const jitter = (rng() - 0.5) * 2 * randomness * spread * 0.6 const lean = asymmetry * spread * 0.5 const next = length * ratio * (1 + (rng() - 0.5) * randomness * 0.4) branch(x2, y2, angle + offset + jitter + lean, next, depth + 1) } } // base case: a leaf (bell) emitReturn(node) // the phrase resolves } ``` | Param | Range | Default | Help text | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | depth | 1–10 (clamped by branching) | 7 | How many times each branch splits. Deeper trees make longer songs. | | branching | 2–4 | 2 | How many new branches grow from each tip. More branches, richer harmony. | | spread | 5–60° | 24° | How wide the branches open. Wider trees sound more spacious. | | ratio | 0.55–0.82 | 0.72 | How much shorter each branch is than its parent. Shorter branches make quicker notes. | | randomness | 0–1 | 0.25 | How much the wind bends each branch. Adds gentle variation. | | asymmetry | -1–1 | 0 | Leans the tree left or right. Shifts the melody up or down. | | seed | text | random words | Same seed, same song. Share it with a friend. | Depth clamp so the full tree fits a 2,047-node budget: branching 2 → max depth 10; 3 → 6; 4 → 5. The depth slider max follows the branching value. Never truncate a tree halfway (lopsided trees sound broken). ### §4.2 World 2: L-System Garden (Should) - Recursive expansion, not string replacement: `expand(symbol, depth)` returns the symbol when `depth === 0` or no rule exists; otherwise it calls `expand` for every symbol in the rule. The expand call stack is the recursion trace (call depth = rewrite depth). - Turtle: `F` draws a segment (one node), `+`/`-` rotate, `[` pushes state (a branch begins), `]` pops (the branch returns). - Presets (axiom, rules, angle, iterations): Fern `X` · `X→F+[[X]-X]-F[-FX]+X`, `F→FF` · 25° · 5; Bush `F` · `F→FF+[+F-F-F]-[-F+F+F]` · 22.5° · 4; Koch snowflake `F++F++F` · `F→F-F++F-F` · 60° · 4; Dragon `FX` · `X→X+YF+`, `Y→-FX-Y` · 90° · 10; Sierpinski arrowhead `A` · `A→B-A-B`, `B→A+B+A` · 60° · 6; Hilbert `A` · `A→+BF-AFA-FB+`, `B→-AF+BFB+FA-` · 90° · 5. - Rule editor: validate symbols, balanced brackets, and a 4,000-segment cap (the iteration slider max adapts per preset). ### §4.3 World 3: Hanoi Music Box (Could) - `hanoi(n, from, to, via)`: if `n === 0` return; `hanoi(n-1, from, via, to)`; `move(n, from, to)`; `hanoi(n-1, via, to, from)`. - Discs 3–8 (default 5 → 31 moves). Discs glide on arcs (700 ms, ease-in-out); a soft ripple on landing. - The smallest disc moves every other step, so its notes form a natural ostinato. The move sequence is a fractal rhythm (the ruler sequence). ### §4.4 Making recursion visible (Should) - Recursion lens: live call stack as indented frames, e.g. `branch(depth 3, len 0.37, θ 102°)`, plus counters (calls, current depth, max depth). - Code view: the world's `codeSnippet` with the executing line highlighted. Call → note, base case → bell, return → resolution. - Depth skyline: a stepped silhouette of call depth over time under the transport bar, with playhead and click/keyboard seek. --- ## §5 Composer (trace → score) ### §5.1 Score model ```ts type Voice = 'drone' | 'pad' | 'lead' | 'ornament' | 'bell' | 'bass'; interface ScoreNote { id: string; time: number; duration: number; midi: number; velocity: number; pan: number; voice: Voice; nodeId: number; depth: number } interface ScoreChord { time: number; duration: number; midis: number[]; symbol: string } interface ScoreEvent { time: number; kind: 'call' | 'return' | 'cadence' | 'section'; nodeId: number; depth: number } interface Score { version: 1; seed: string; worldId: WorldId; moodId: MoodId; mode: 'wander' | 'bloom'; bpm: number; key: string; scale: ScaleId; duration: number; tail: number; // seconds notes: ScoreNote[]; chords: ScoreChord[]; events: ScoreEvent[]; stats: { noteCount: number; nodeCount: number; maxDepth: number }; } ``` Times are in seconds from 0. Velocity is 0–1. Pan is -1 to 1. The composer is pure and deterministic. ### §5.2 Scales (semitones from the root) majorPentatonic `[0,2,4,7,9]` · minorPentatonic `[0,3,5,7,10]` · yo `[0,2,5,7,9]` · lydian `[0,2,4,6,7,9,11]` · dorian `[0,2,3,5,7,9,10]` · aeolian `[0,2,3,5,7,8,10]` · ionian `[0,2,4,5,7,9,11]`. Melody arithmetic happens in scale degrees (an index into the scale across octaves), so every note is in the scale by construction. ### §5.3 Fractal form (the core idea) | Recursion level | Musical role | Voice | | --- | --- | --- | | Trunk (depth 0) | the key; a root + fifth drone for the whole piece | drone | | Boughs (depth 1) | sections A, B (C, D) of the piece | section events, pad colour | | Depth 2 | phrases; each depth-2 subtree is one phrase with one chord from the mood's progression (cycled) | pad | | Depth 3 to maxDepth-2 | the melody | lead | | Twigs (maxDepth-1) | ornaments: quieter, higher, thinned by density | ornament | | Leaves (base case) | bells: chord tones, upper octave, long ring | bell | | Return from a depth-2 call | cadence: soft pad re-swell + one beat of rest | pad | | Return from the root | final cadence to the tonic + 8–12 s tail | pad, drone | For shallow trees (maxDepth ≤ 3) the melody starts at depth 1. The last phrase always ends on the tonic chord. ### §5.4 Wander (depth-first, default) - Walk the trace events in order. A `call` at depth ≥ 3 emits a lead note; twigs emit ornaments; leaves emit bells. - Beat = 60 / bpm seconds. Lead duration in beats = quantise(lerp(0.5, 2, sqrt(length / trunkLength))) to {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2}. Ornaments 0.5 beat. Bells ring 4 beats but advance the cursor only 0.5 beat. - Pitch: degree(child) = degree(parent) + step. For branching 2, left child +0 and right child +2 (a gentle climb toward the leaves); for 3–4 children, steps spread across -1…+2. Branch jitter adds ±1 degree with probability = randomness × 0.5 (seeded). - At a phrase start, snap to the nearest chord tone. On strong beats (1 and 3 of 4/4), move non-chord tones to the nearest chord tone. - Lead range MIDI 60–84 (reflect at the edges). Never repeat one pitch more than 3 times in a row. - Bells: the chord tone nearest to lead + 12, clamped to MIDI 72–96. ### §5.5 Bloom (breadth-first, Should) - Level 0 starts the drone; level 1 swells the first chord; each level d ≥ 2 becomes a 2-bar phrase. - Nodes in a level are sorted by x (left → right, like a harp sweep) and spread across the phrase with seeded offsets of ±0.15 beat. - Pitches come from the current chord; register rises one step per level. The chord progression advances once per level. - Cap 12 notes per phrase. Pick a seeded, evenly spaced subset when a level is larger. End with a return to the tonic. ### §5.6 Dynamics, density, humanisation, length - Velocity = clamp(0.62 × 0.92^depth × form(t) × (1 ± 0.08 seeded), 0.12, 0.85). `form(t)` rises 0.7 → 1.0 over the first 25% of the piece, holds to 70%, and falls to 0.75 at the end. - Density cap: at most `mood.maxNotesPerSecond` (default 3.5) in any 1 s window. Drop lowest priority first: ornaments, then bells, then lead (never drone or pad). - Humanise onsets ±12 ms (lead), ±20 ms (bells). Never below 0. - Target length 90 s–6 min. If longer, raise tempo up to +15% then thin the deepest level. If shorter, slow down to the mood's minimum tempo. ### §5.7 Mappings for other worlds - L-System: each `F` is a note; `+`/`-` move one scale degree up/down; `[` saves pitch and starts a quieter harmony voice one register up; `]` restores the saved pitch (melodic return). Bracket depth lowers velocity by 8% per level. Rewrite depth chooses the voice (shallow = lead, deep = ornament). - Hanoi: disc n → degree (N − n) (larger discs lower); peg → pan (-0.6, 0, 0.6) and voice (pluck, lead, bell); one move per beat; call depth → velocity. ### §5.8 Endless Drift (Could) After a piece ends, generate the next seed, modulate to the key a fifth up (circle of fifths), and crossfade over 8 s. --- ## §6 Sound design ### §6.1 Moods | Mood | Root, scale | BPM | Progression (pad) | Lead | Ambience | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Dawn Mist | D, majorPentatonic (harmony from D major) | 60 | Dadd9 – Bm7 – Gmaj7 – Asus4 → D | soft FM electric piano | birds + breeze | | Rain Garden | A, minorPentatonic (harmony from A aeolian) | 56 | Am(add9) – Fmaj7 – C – G → Am | FM kalimba pluck | rain | | Deep Ocean | C, lydian | 50 | Cmaj7 – D/C – Em7 – Cmaj7(#11) | sparse glass bells + pad swells | ocean waves | | Night Forest | F♯, minorPentatonic | 54 | F♯m – D – A – Esus2 → F♯m | harp-like Karplus–Strong pluck | crickets + stream | | Temple | D, yo | 48 | open fifths and fourths over a D drone (no functional progression) | koto-like pluck | wind + distant chimes | In Deep Ocean the F♯ (Lydian 4th) may only appear as a short note on a weak beat. ### §6.2 Voices (Tone.js v15 starting patches; tune by ear) - # Seedsong starter kit: set up in 20 minutes

This kit turns an empty repo into a fully briefed Claude Code project: the spec, the prompt chain, project skills, review agents, MCP servers and automatic AI logging. Install it BEFORE your first prompt so every prompt is logged.

## What is in the kit

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Project brain Claude Code reads every session: rubric, stack, rules, definition of done |
| `docs/SPEC.md` | The full product and technical spec (what to build, exactly) |
| `docs/PROMPTS.md` | The prompt chain, phase by phase, plus feedback templates |
| `docs/RUBRIC.md` | Official rubric, what a 10/10 looks like, final self-check |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Safe permission allowlist + 4 logging hooks |
| `.claude/hooks/ai-log.mjs` | Logs every prompt and response to `ai-logs/` |
| `.claude/skills/` | `verify` (auto-runs before commits), `sound-design`, `calm-ux`, `judge` |
| `.claude/agents/` | `rubric-judge`, `a11y-auditor`, `music-director` (independent reviewers) |
| `.mcp.json` / `.mcp.windows.json` | Playwright (Claude's eyes in the browser) + Context7 (live library docs) |
| `scripts/collect-ai-logs.mjs` | Collects every Claude Code transcript for the repo into `ai-logs/` |
| `ai-logs/` | Where the logs live, plus the planning session |

## 1. Prerequisites

- Node.js LTS (nodejs.org) and Git. On Windows, Git for Windows is recommended (it gives Claude Code a Bash shell).
- A GitHub account and an empty public repo (for example `seedsong`).
- Google Chrome, and headphones.

## 2. Install or update Claude Code

- macOS / Linux / WSL: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`
- Windows PowerShell: `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`
- Already installed: `claude update`. Check with `claude --version`.

## 3. Put the kit in your repo

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/seedsong.git
cd seedsong
# unzip the kit INTO this folder so CLAUDE.md sits at the top level
# make sure the hidden .claude folder and .mcp.json came along
```

**Windows only:** delete `.mcp.json` and rename `.mcp.windows.json` to `.mcp.json` (npx needs the `cmd /c` wrapper on native Windows).

Commit it:

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "chore: add Claude Code starter kit (spec, prompt chain, skills, logging hooks)"
git push
```

## 4. Start Claude Code and finish setup

```bash
claude
```

1. Trust the folder, and approve the project MCP servers `playwright` and `context7` when asked.
2. Install the official frontend-design plugin:
   ```
   /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official
   /plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official
   /reload-plugins
   ```
   (If the first line says the marketplace already exists, that is fine.)
3. Optional: `/plugin marketplace add nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill` then `/plugin install ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill`. Use it for its UX and accessibility checklists only; its colour and layout suggestions lean toward marketing landing pages, and SPEC §7 already defines our look.
4. Check everything loaded:
   - `/hooks` shows UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop and SessionEnd.
   - `/mcp` shows playwright and context7 connected.
   - `/skills` lists verify, sound-design, calm-ux, judge and frontend-design.
5. Logging smoke test. Send: `Say hello in one line and list the project skills and agents you can see.` Then open `ai-logs/PROMPT_LOG.md`: you should see Prompt 1 and the response. Delete nothing in `ai-logs/`, ever.
6. Pick the model and effort for Phase 0: `/model best` (it picks Fable where your plan includes it, otherwise the latest Opus), then `/effort xhigh`.
7. Open `docs/PROMPTS.md` and start with Phase 0.

## 5. Troubleshooting

- **No entries in `ai-logs/PROMPT_LOG.md`:** run `node --version` (Node must be on PATH), check `/hooks`, and read `ai-logs/.hook-errors.log`. If your Claude Code build rejects the `args` form, change each hook to the shell form, for example `"command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/ai-log.mjs\" prompt"` and remove `args`.
- **Logs are still safe if hooks failed:** `npm run logs:collect` (or `node scripts/collect-ai-logs.mjs`) rebuilds them from Claude Code's own transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/`. Run it before every push in the last hours.
- **Playwright MCP does not connect on Windows:** confirm you renamed `.mcp.windows.json`, then `/mcp` → reconnect.
- **Usage limit reached:** `/usage` shows when it resets. Switch lighter phases to `/model sonnet`. If you must switch to another AI tool, save its full prompt/response history into `ai-logs/` by hand.
- **Never** let any tool scaffold with `--overwrite` into this folder; Phase 1 scaffolds into `_scaffold/` and merges.
# Official rubric (Hub's Quest Epoch 1, "Recursive Soundscapes")

Source: the challenge brief PDF. Solo, 24 hours, any AI coding agent allowed, but the repo must contain the full prompt chain and the agent's response to each prompt.

## Mandatory deliverables (all six must work in the deployed build)

1. A functional recursive algorithm with configurable parameters.
2. An interactive simulation or visualization.
3. A procedural music-generation system that uses the recursive process.
4. A user interface with parameter controls and audio playback.
5. A working audio export feature.
6. A polished, accessible experience designed around relaxation and enjoyment.

Guiding principle from the brief: "Make recursion audible. Make simulation beautiful. Make the experience relaxing."

## Scoring weights and what a 10/10 looks like

| Criterion | Weight | 10/10 looks like | Common ways to lose points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Relaxation & user experience | 35% | Within 10 seconds a stranger feels calmer. One tap to a finished piece. Nothing startles: fades everywhere, soft colours, slow motion. Works on a phone. Breathing, zen and sleep-timer tools feel native. | Abrupt starts or stops, clicks, loud peaks, busy UI, walls of sliders up front, tiny targets, broken mobile layout, jargon |
| Musical quality | 25% | Sounds like intentional ambient music: consonant harmony that moves, a melody with shape, phrases that breathe and resolve, warm timbres, a clean mix, no fatigue after 10 minutes. | Random pitches, out-of-key notes, square-wave harshness, mud in the low end, too many notes, no form, clipping |
| Creative use of recursion | 15% | The recursion's structure is audibly the musical structure (form, phrases, cadences on returns). Users can see which call is playing and hear depth-first vs breadth-first. More than one recursion. | Recursion only used to produce a list of numbers mapped to pitch; recursion invisible in the UI |
| Visual design | 10% | A coherent, distinctive look (tokens, type, palette per mood); the simulation is beautiful and synced to sound; 60 fps. | Generic template look, default component styling, desync, jank, flashing |
| Interaction & usability | 10% | Obvious controls with plain-language help, presets, keyboard shortcuts, shareable seeds, undo-safe changes, helpful empty and error states. | Unlabelled sliders, hidden features, no feedback on long actions (export), lost settings |
| Technical execution | 5% | Clean architecture, tests and CI, deployed demo, reliable export, no console errors, good performance, clear README. | Crashes, export that fails or is silent, memory leaks, no README |

## Self-check before submitting

- [ ] All six mandatory deliverables work on the deployed URL in a fresh browser profile.
- [ ] First minute: Begin → drone fades in → tree grows in sync → piece resolves. No console errors.
- [ ] Every mood sounds calm and consonant for 5 minutes on headphones and on phone speakers.
- [ ] Export WAV and MIDI work; the files open in a normal player or DAW.
- [ ] Keyboard-only run-through works; axe reports 0 serious/critical violations; reduced motion works.
- [ ] README has the live link, video link, mapping table, deliverables list, credits and AI-usage section.
- [ ] `ai-logs/` contains PROMPT_LOG.md, transcripts for every session, INDEX.md and the planning session.

# AI usage logs

Seedsong was built for Hub's Quest Epoch 1 with Claude Code as the coding agent. The rules require the full prompt chain and the agent's response to each prompt, so everything is recorded here automatically.

| Path | What it is | How it is made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROMPT_LOG.md` | Every prompt in order, with the agent's final response, files changed and commands run | Written live by the hooks in `.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/hooks/ai-log.mjs`) |
| `prompt-log.jsonl` | The same events as machine-readable JSON lines | Same hooks |
| `transcripts/` | Raw Claude Code transcripts (JSONL), including subagents and every tool call | Copied by the hooks after each turn and by `npm run logs:collect` |
| `sessions/` | A readable Markdown transcript of every session | `npm run logs:collect` |
| `INDEX.md` | A table of all sessions with links | `npm run logs:collect` |
| `00-planning/` | The planning conversation (claude.ai) that produced the spec, the prompt chain and this logging setup | Exported by hand |

Method in one line: a written spec (`docs/SPEC.md`) and a phase-by-phase prompt chain (`docs/PROMPTS.md`), each phase planned, implemented, verified with tests and browser screenshots, listened to by the human, and committed.

2. This starter kit: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/PROMPTS.md`, `docs/RUBRIC.md`, project skills (`verify`, `sound-design`, `calm-ux`, `judge`), review agents (`rubric-judge`, `a11y-auditor`, `music-director`), the logging hooks and `scripts/collect-ai-logs.mjs`.

# Verify (Seedsong)

1. Run `npm run verify` (typecheck, lint, unit tests, build). Fix every failure at its cause. Never skip, delete or weaken a test to get green.
2. If anything under `src/ui`, `src/viz`, `src/audio`, `src/export`, `src/styles` or `index.html` changed:
   - Run `npm run test:e2e`.
   - Start the dev server if it is not running, open it with the Playwright MCP, click Begin, let it play for 5 seconds, and confirm the console has no errors or warnings from our code.
   - Take a screenshot at 1440×900 (and 390×844 if layout changed) and look at it critically against `docs/SPEC.md` §7 and §8.
3. If `src/core/music`, `src/audio` or `src/export` changed and `npm run audio:qa` exists, run it and quote its summary table.
4. Report in five lines or fewer: commands run and results, screenshots taken, anything suspicious, and what the user should listen for (you cannot hear audio).

Do not commit if step 1 or step 2 fails. Never touch `ai-logs/` or `.claude/hooks/`.

5. **Commit every green phase.** The `verify` skill runs before each commit. Push after every phase so CI deploys a live build.
6. **Watch usage.** Run `/usage` between phases. Above about 70% of your window, switch to `/model sonnet` for the lighter phases listed below.

| Phase | Model | Effort | Mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 Architecture | `/model best` (Fable where your plan has it, otherwise Opus) | xhigh | plan |
| 1 Scaffold | opus | high | accept edits |
| 2 Recursion engine | opus | high | accept edits |
| 3 Composer | best | xhigh | plan → accept edits |
| 4 Audio engine | best | high | accept edits |
| 5 Export | opus | high | accept edits |
| 6 Visualizer | opus | high | accept edits |
| 7 Relaxation UX | best | high | plan → accept edits |

| 9 Extra worlds | opus or sonnet | high | accept edits |
