```
/plan We are building "Seedsong" for a 24-hour solo hackathon (deadline Thu 26 Nov 2026, 22:00 GMT+6). Read CLAUDE.md, docs/SPEC.md (all of it) and docs/RUBRIC.md before answering.

Produce a plan that I will save as docs/plans/00-architecture.md, containing:
1. The folder and module structure from SPEC §10, changed only where you have a concrete reason (say why).
2. Exact TypeScript interfaces for WorldDefinition, ParamSpec, RecursionTrace, TraceNode, MusicParams, Mood, Score, ScoreNote, ScoreChord, ScoreEvent, and the AudioEngine public API.
3. A mermaid data-flow diagram: user params → trace → score → live playback / offline export / MIDI / visuals.
4. The dependency list with versions you verified with `npm view <pkg> version`. Keep the create-vite defaults (oxlint, TypeScript 7). No ESLint.
5. The 8 biggest technical risks (for example Tone.Offline with Reverb readiness, iOS silent switch, canvas performance, GitHub Pages base path) and the mitigation for each.
6. A checklist for Phases 1–12 of docs/PROMPTS.md with acceptance criteria per phase.

Do not write application code yet. Ask me at most 3 questions, and only if something blocks the plan.
```

```
Implement Phase 1 of docs/plans/00-architecture.md.

Begin calls Tone.start(), sets navigator.audioSession.type = "playback" when available, and plays a soft 3-second Dadd9 pad through a limiter with a fade in and out. Keyboard accessible, visible focus.

```

# Seedsong **Plant a seed. Watch recursion grow. Listen to it bloom.** A calm browser “sound garden” for Hub’s Quest Epoch 1 · *Recursive Soundscapes*. A recursive function grows a glowing tree, and the **call tree itself becomes the music**: every call is a note, every leaf (base case) rings a bell, and every return resolves a phrase. **Live demo:** _add your GitHub Pages URL here_ · **Video:** _add your demo video link here_
--- ## The idea Most “math music” maps numbers to random pitches. Seedsong maps **the shape of the recursion** to **the shape of the music**. A tree already has the structure of a piece: one root, a few big sections, many small phrases, and endings. So each level of `branch()` gets a musical job, and each `return` resolves what its call started. | Recursion | Music | What you hear | | --- | --- | --- | | Trunk (the first call, depth 0) | The key | a root + fifth drone under the whole piece | | Boughs (depth 1) | Sections | the melody moves to a new register | | Depth-2 calls | Phrases | each phrase gets one chord from the mood’s progression, voice-led | | Inner branches | Melody | longer branches play longer notes; left steps down, right climbs | | Twigs (max depth − 1) | Ornaments | quieter, higher grace notes | | Leaves (the **base case**) | Bells | chord tones an octave up; a blossom opens on the tree | | Return from a phrase | Cadence | one beat of rest while the pad swells | | Return from the root | Ending | the home chord and a long tail | Other properties map too: branch **length → note length and loudness**, branch **angle → melodic step**, branch **x position → stereo pan**, **depth → register and softness**, and the **seed → the whole piece** (same seed, same song). Two ways to walk the same tree, one toggle: - **Wander (depth-first):** the melody climbs one branch to its leaf, returns, and climbs the next, like an improvisation that keeps coming home. - **Bloom (breadth-first):** each level plays as one phrase, left to right like a harp sweep, so the tree blooms from drone to bells. Hearing the difference teaches DFS vs BFS faster than any diagram. Even the harp sound is recursive: it is a Karplus–Strong pluck, a feedback loop. ## The six mandatory deliverables | # | Deliverable | Where it lives | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Recursive algorithm with configurable parameters | **Fractal Grove** `branch(x, y, angle, length, depth)` (`src/core/worlds/grove.ts`): depth, branches, spread, taper, wind, lean, seed. **L-System Garden** `grow(symbol, depth)` (`src/core/worlds/lsystem.ts`): six plants, generations, bend, wind, lean. Drawer → *World* tab. | | 2 | Interactive simulation / visualization | Canvas renderer (`src/viz/renderer.ts`): the tree grows branch by branch in sync with its notes, blossoms open when their bell rings, wind sway, fireflies. Plus the **recursion lens** (live call stack, counters, running line of code) and the **depth skyline** timeline you can click to seek. | | 3 | Procedural music from the recursive process | Composer (`src/core/music/compose.ts`): pure, deterministic `RecursionTrace → Score` with scale lock, voice-leading, cadences on returns, density cap, Wander and Bloom. | | 4 | UI with parameter controls and audio playback | Play/pause, seek, volume, mute, five mood presets, Wander/Bloom, new seed, drawer with World / Sound / Atmosphere / Session tabs, keyboard shortcuts. | | 5 | Working audio export | **Keep this song**: WAV (16- or 24-bit, offline-rendered with the same instruments, dithered, peak-normalised, metadata with the share link), MP3 (192 kbps, Web Worker), MIDI (one track per voice), and 1600×1600 cover art. Real progress bar. | | 6 | Polished, accessible, relaxing experience | One-tap Begin ritual, five moods with 3 s crossfades, procedural ambience mixer, breathing companion, sleep timer, zen mode, endless garden, reduced-motion mode, WCAG 2.2 AA checks (axe: 0 serious/critical). | ## Features by rubric line **Relaxation & UX (35%)**: a first minute designed as a ritual (headphones hint → one *Begin* → drone fades in over 6 s → the trunk grows). Nothing startles: every start, stop, seek and regenerate is ramped (dip-crossfades, 400 ms debounce on sliders). Breathing companion (4 s in, 6 s out), sleep timer (15/30/60 min with a 60 s fade), zen mode, endless garden, eight procedural ambience layers (rain, ocean, wind, stream, crickets, birds, fire, chimes). Calm copy, no exclamation marks. Works on phones (bottom-sheet drawer, 44 px targets). **Musical quality (25%)**: every melody note is computed in scale degrees, so out-of-key notes are impossible by construction. # Build decisions (and where they differ from the spec)

The spec (`docs/SPEC.md`) was written before any code. These are the places the build deliberately differs, and why.

| Spec | Build | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tailwind CSS 4 + Radix UI + Motion | Plain CSS with design tokens (`src/styles/app.css`), native elements (`<input type="range">`, `<dialog>`, `role="tablist"`), CSS animations | Fewer moving parts in a 24-hour build, a smaller bundle (181 KB gzipped JS), and native controls are accessible by default (keyboard, focus trap, `aria-valuetext`). The visual token system from SPEC §7.1 is unchanged. |
| `compose.worker.ts` (generate + compose off the main thread) | Main thread | The largest tree (2,047 nodes) generates and composes in about 8 ms, well under the 50 ms budget, so a worker adds complexity for no gain. |
| Visual sync via `getDraw().schedule()` events | The renderer reads the audible transport time every frame and derives growth, highlights and blossoms from the Score | Same audio clock, no drift, and seeking or pausing needs no event replay. The renderer still never schedules audio. |
| Pause by stopping the transport | Pause fades out, then suspends the AudioContext | Every envelope and the transport freeze exactly where they are, so resuming is seamless (no re-triggering). |
| Crossfade two racks on regenerate | Dip-crossfade: fade out 1.1 s, swap, fade in 1.6 s | Half the CPU, and it still never cuts. Mood changes build the new rack before the old one is released, and old racks are disposed after their reverb tails. |
| `Tone.Offline()` for export | A hand-built `OfflineContext` with the same steps | Tone's clock loop yields with `setTimeout` once per second of audio, which background tabs throttle to about 1 s per yield. This loop yields with a `MessageChannel`, and `OfflineAudioContext.suspend()` checkpoints give a real progress bar. |
| Reverb decay 9 s, pad `fattriangle` × 3 | Decay 7 s, × 2 | Offline rendering was dominated by these nodes; this keeps the sound lush and makes export noticeably faster. |
| Hanoi Music Box (Could) | Not built | Two recursions (Grove and L-System) cover “more than one recursion”; time went to sound, UX and tests instead. |
| L-System presets include Koch, Dragon, Sierpinski, Hilbert | Branching plants only (Fern, Willow, Sprig, Reed, Bush, Lantern) | The music is built from the bracket tree (`[` = call, `]` = return). Curves without brackets have no branching structure, so they would be one long phrase. “Garden” plants keep the mapping honest. |

## Timing safety (a bug found by the e2e tests)

When the song regrows, notes from the old transport that were already handed to the audio graph (inside the 0.12 s look-ahead) can still start after the new transport begins. A voice could then receive a start time earlier than one it already had, and Tone throws. The engine now releases voices and restarts the transport only after the look-ahead window (`settled()`, `startOffset` in `src/audio/engine.ts`).

| L-System presets include Koch, Dragon, Sierpinski, Hilbert | Branching plants only (Fern, Willow, Sprig, Reed, Bush, Lantern) | The music is built from the bracket tree (`[` = call, `]` = return). Curves without brackets have no branching structure, so they would be one long phrase. “Garden” plants keep the mapping honest. |

## Timing safety (a bug found by the e2e tests)

When the song regrows, notes from the old transport that were already handed to the audio graph (inside the 0.12 s look-ahead) can still start after the new transport begins. A voice could then receive a start time earlier than one it already had, and Tone throws. The engine now releases voices and restarts the transport only after the look-ahead window (`settled()`, `startOffset` in `src/audio/engine.ts`).

# Seedsong **Plant a seed. Watch recursion grow. Listen to it bloom.** A calm browser “sound garden” for Hub’s Quest Epoch 1 · *Recursive Soundscapes*. A recursive function grows a glowing tree, and the **call tree itself becomes the music**: every call is a note, every leaf (base case) rings a bell, and every return resolves a phrase. **Live demo:** _add your GitHub Pages URL here_ · **Video:** _add your demo video link here_
--- ## The idea Most “math music” maps numbers to random pitches. Seedsong maps **the shape of the recursion** to **the shape of the music**. A tree already has the structure of a piece: one root, a few big sections, many small phrases, and endings. So each level of `branch()` gets a musical job, and each `return` resolves what its call started. | Recursion | Music | What you hear | | --- | --- | --- | | Trunk (the first call, depth 0) | The key | a root + fifth drone under the whole piece | | Boughs (depth 1) | Sections | the melody moves to a new register | | Depth-2 calls | Phrases | each phrase gets one chord from the mood’s progression, voice-led | | Inner branches | Melody | longer branches play longer notes; left steps down, right climbs | | Twigs (max depth − 1) | Ornaments | quieter, higher grace notes | | Leaves (the **base case**) | Bells | chord tones an octave up; a blossom opens on the tree | | Return from a phrase | Cadence | one beat of rest while the pad swells | | Return from the root | Ending | the home chord and a long tail | Other properties map too: branch **length → note length and loudness**, branch **angle → melodic step**, branch **x position → stereo pan**, **depth → register and softness**, and the **seed → the whole piece** (same seed, same song). Two ways to walk the same tree, one toggle: - **Wander (depth-first):** the melody climbs one branch to its leaf, returns, and climbs the next, like an improvisation that keeps coming home. - **Bloom (breadth-first):** each level plays as one phrase, left to right like a harp sweep, so the tree blooms from drone to bells. Hearing the difference teaches DFS vs BFS faster than any diagram. Even the harp sound is recursive: it is a Karplus–Strong pluck, a feedback loop. ## The six mandatory deliverables | # | Deliverable | Where it lives | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Recursive algorithm with configurable parameters | **Fractal Grove** `branch(x, y, angle, length, depth)` (`src/core/worlds/grove.ts`): depth, branches, spread, taper, wind, lean, seed. **L-System Garden** `grow(symbol, depth)` (`src/core/worlds/lsystem.ts`): six plants, generations, bend, wind, lean. Drawer → *World* tab. | | 2 | Interactive simulation / visualization | Canvas renderer (`src/viz/renderer.ts`): the tree grows branch by branch in sync with its notes, blossoms open when their bell rings, wind sway, fireflies. Plus the **recursion lens** (live call stack, counters, running line of code) and the **depth skyline** timeline you can click to seek. | | 3 | Procedural music from the recursive process | Composer (`src/core/music/compose.ts`): pure, deterministic `RecursionTrace → Score` with scale lock, voice-leading, cadences on returns, density cap, Wander and Bloom. | | 4 | UI with parameter controls and audio playback | Play/pause, seek, volume, mute, five mood presets, Wander/Bloom, new seed, drawer with World / Sound / Atmosphere / Session tabs, keyboard shortcuts. | | 5 | Working audio export | **Keep this song**: WAV (16- or 24-bit, offline-rendered with the same instruments, dithered, peak-normalised, metadata with the share link), MP3 (192 kbps, Web Worker), MIDI (one track per voice), and 1600×1600 cover art. Real progress bar. | | 6 | Polished, accessible, relaxing experience | One-tap Begin ritual, five moods with 3 s crossfades, procedural ambience mixer, breathing companion, sleep timer, zen mode, endless garden, reduced-motion mode, WCAG 2.2 AA checks (axe: 0 serious/critical). | ## Features by rubric line **Relaxation & UX (35%)**: a first minute designed as a ritual (headphones hint → one *Begin* → drone fades in over 6 s → the trunk grows). Nothing startles: every start, stop, seek and regenerate is ramped (dip-crossfades, 400 ms debounce on sliders). Breathing companion (4 s in, 6 s out), sleep timer (15/30/60 min with a 60 s fade), zen mode, endless garden, eight procedural ambience layers (rain, ocean, wind, stream, crickets, birds, fire, chimes). Calm copy, no exclamation marks. Works on phones (bottom-sheet drawer, 44 px targets). **Musical quality (25%)**: every melody note is computed in scale degrees, so out-of-key notes are impossible by construction. Chords move every phrase and are voice-led for the smallest movement. Phrases breathe (cadence + rest on each depth-2 return), the piece ends on the tonic with a tail. Density is capped (≤ 3.5 attacked notes in any second). Seeded humanisation (±12–20 ms, ±8% velocity). A real mix: high-passed voices, one long convolution reverb on a send, dotted-eighth delay, EQ → compressor → makeup → limiter at −1 dB. `npm run audio:qa` renders every mood and mode and checks the result (see below). **Creative use of recursion (15%)**: the call tree *is* the form; the lens shows the live call stack and highlights the running line of code (call → note, base case → bell, return → resolution); the depth skyline shows the recursion’s shape over time; Wander vs Bloom; two different recursions (a branching function and a recursive grammar rewrite). **Visual design (10%)**: one token system (“Nocturne Garden”: ink-navy sky, glass panels, Fraunces / Manrope / JetBrains Mono), a palette per mood that crossfades with the music, bioluminescent branches (trunk → tip gradient + additive glow), blossoms and sparks on bells, 60 fps Canvas 2D with batched paths. **Interaction & usability (10%)**: plain-language help under every slider (“Depth: how many times each branch splits. Deeper trees make longer songs.”), presets first and parameters on request, shortcuts (Space, N, W, L, Z, E, M, ←/→, ↑/↓, 1–5, ?), share links that regrow the exact song, a local garden of saved seeds, gentle toasts and a *Replant* error screen. **Technical execution (5%)**: pure, tested core; one rack for live and offline; unit + end-to-end + accessibility tests; audio QA; CI and GitHub Pages deploy workflows; 181 KB gzipped JS. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Parameters + seed] --> W["World.generate()
(real recursion)"] W --> T[RecursionTrace
nodes + call/return events] T --> C["composeScore()
Wander / Bloom"] M[Mood] --> C C --> S[Score
notes · chords · events · node timings] S --> L[Live engine
Tone.js transport] S --> O[Offline render
same createRack] S --> X[MIDI] S --> V[Canvas renderer
reads the audible time] S --> K[Recursion lens
+ depth skyline] O --> WAV[WAV / MP3] V --> PNG[Cover art] ``` - `src/core/**` is pure TypeScript (no DOM, no Tone, no React) and deterministic for a given (params, seed). Randomness only comes from a seeded PRNG (`cyrb128` → `sfc32`). - `src/audio/rack.ts` has **one** `createRack()` used by live playback **and** by the offline export, so the file sounds like what you heard. - The visuals never schedule audio. Each frame reads the audible transport time and derives what has grown and what is sounding from the Score, so sight and sound cannot drift (and seeking just works). ``` src/ core/ random.ts, url.ts (share links) worlds/ types.ts, grove.ts, lsystem.ts, registry.ts music/ theory.ts, moods.ts, score.ts, compose.ts (+ core.test.ts) audio/ rack.ts, engine.ts, schedule.ts export/ offline.ts, wav.ts, mp3.ts + mp3.worker.ts, midi.ts, cover.ts, download.ts viz/ renderer.ts, color.ts ui/ components/ (Landing, TopBar, Dock, Drawer, Lens, KeepDialog, HelpDialog, Breathing, Toasts, Modal), hooks.ts state/ store.ts (Zustand) app/ App.tsx, controller.ts, ErrorBoundary.tsx tests/e2e/ smoke, export, a11y (Playwright + axe) scripts/ audio-qa.mjs, collect-ai-logs.mjs ``` ## Run it Requires Node.js 22+. ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 npm run verify # typecheck + lint + unit tests + build npm run test:e2e # Playwright: smoke, keyboard, export, accessibility (uses Microsoft Edge locally) npm run audio:qa # renders every mood × mode offline and checks the mix npm run build # static site in dist/ (relative base, works on any GitHub Pages path) ``` **Deploy:** push to `main` on GitHub, then *Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions*. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds and publishes; `ci.yml` runs verify + e2e. ## Quality evidence Measured on this build: - Unit tests: 24 passing (determinism, node counts, call/return nesting, scale lock for every mood and mode, density cap, tonic ending, length budget, share links). The largest tree (2,047 nodes) generates and composes in about 8 ms. - End-to-end: Begin → plays with no console errors (desktop and phone viewports); keyboard shortcuts; a real WAV download (about 10.6 MB, RMS −17 dBFS); axe on every screen state with 0 serious/critical violations. - Audio QA (`npm run audio:qa`), reference seed `still-lake-07`, all five moods × both modes: peaks −3.6 to −5.8 dBFS (no clipping), RMS about −19 to −20 dBFS live, about −15 to −16.5 dBFS after export normalisation (target −18 to −16 LUFS), no silence longer than 0.1 s before the outro. ## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) Full keyboard operation with visible focus; native `` focus traps; single-key shortcuts can be turned off and never fire inside inputs; sliders announce values with units (`aria-valuetext`); the canvas has a live text description (“A fractal tree, 255 branches, 7 levels deep, playing in D major pentatonic at 60 BPM…”); toasts are polite live regions; reduced-motion mode (system or in-app) removes sway, drift and zoom; nothing flashes; audio never autoplays; a mono switch for single-sided hearing; 44 px touch targets; layouts reflow to 320 px. ## Design decisions grounded in research - Relaxing music tends to be legato, unaccented, soft (pp–mp), smooth in contour, repetitive, mid-register and thin in texture (web listening study of 293 adults; Conrad et al., *medRxiv* preprint, 2023). The composer’s rules (soft velocities, long releases, stepwise melody, density cap, mid-register lead) follow these findings. - People relax differently: a study that slowed tempo to 45 BPM and softened timbre found two distinct responder profiles (Hernández-Ruiz et al., *Psychology of Music*, 2020). That is why there are five moods and a user tempo control (40–96 BPM). ## Credits and licences See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). Code: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). All sound is synthesised in the browser; no samples are shipped. ## AI usage Built solo with **Claude Code** (Anthropic) as the coding agent, following a written spec and prompt chain. The full prompt chain and the agent’s responses are in [`ai-logs/`](ai-logs/): the planning conversation (`ai-logs/00-planning/`), the build session transcripts (`ai-logs/transcripts/`, readable copies in `ai-logs/sessions/`) and an index (`ai-logs/INDEX.md`). See [ai-logs/README.md](ai-logs/README.md).

# Build decisions (and where they differ from the spec)

The spec (`docs/SPEC.md`) was written before any code. These are the places the build deliberately differs, and why.

| Spec | Build | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tailwind CSS 4 + Radix UI + Motion | Plain CSS with design tokens (`src/styles/app.css`), native elements (`<input type="range">`, `<dialog>`, `role="tablist"`), CSS animations | Fewer moving parts in a 24-hour build, a smaller bundle (181 KB gzipped JS), and native controls are accessible by default (keyboard, focus trap, `aria-valuetext`). The visual token system from SPEC §7.1 is unchanged. |
| `compose.worker.ts` (generate + compose off the main thread) | Main thread | The largest tree (2,047 nodes) generates and composes in about 8 ms, well under the 50 ms budget, so a worker adds complexity for no gain. |
| Visual sync via `getDraw().schedule()` events | The renderer reads the audible transport time every frame and derives growth, highlights and blossoms from the Score | Same audio clock, no drift, and seeking or pausing needs no event replay. The renderer still never schedules audio. |
| Pause by stopping the transport | Pause fades out, then suspends the AudioContext | Every envelope and the transport freeze exactly where they are, so resuming is seamless (no re-triggering). |
| Crossfade two racks on regenerate | Dip-crossfade: fade out 1.1 s, swap, fade in 1.6 s | Half the CPU, and it still never cuts. Mood changes build the new rack before the old one is released, and old racks are disposed after their reverb tails. |
| `Tone.Offline()` for export | A hand-built `OfflineContext` with the same steps | Tone's clock loop yields with `setTimeout` once per second of audio, which background tabs throttle to about 1 s per yield. This loop yields with a `MessageChannel`, and `OfflineAudioContext.suspend()` checkpoints give a real progress bar. |
| Reverb decay 9 s, pad `fattriangle` × 3 | Decay 7 s, × 2 | Offline rendering was dominated by these nodes; this keeps the sound lush and makes export noticeably faster. |
| Hanoi Music Box (Could) | Not built | Two recursions (Grove and L-System) cover “more than one recursion”; time went to sound, UX and tests instead. |
| L-System presets include Koch, Dragon, Sierpinski, Hilbert | Branching plants only (Fern, Willow, Sprig, Reed, Bush, Lantern) | The music is built from the bracket tree (`[` = call, `]` = return). Curves without brackets have no branching structure, so they would be one long phrase. “Garden” plants keep the mapping honest. |

## Timing safety (a bug found by the e2e tests)

When the song regrows, notes from the old transport that were already handed to the audio graph (inside the 0.12 s look-ahead) can still start after the new transport begins. A voice could then receive a start time earlier than one it already had, and Tone throws. The engine now releases voices and restarts the transport only after the look-ahead window (`settled()`, `startOffset` in `src/audio/engine.ts`).

# Seedsong: Recursive Soundscapes (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Solo 24-hour hackathon build. Hard deadline: **Thu 26 Nov 2026, 22:00 GMT+6**. Feature freeze: **18:30 GMT+6**.
Seedsong is a browser app where a recursive function grows a glowing fractal tree and the call tree itself becomes relaxing music.
The full product and technical spec is `docs/SPEC.md`. Read the section a task names before you start it. The official rubric and what a 10/10 looks like are in `docs/RUBRIC.md`.

## How we are judged (optimise in this order)

| Weight | Criterion | What it means for every decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 35% | Relaxation & UX | a calm first minute, no harsh sound or motion, frictionless controls, mobile works |
| 25% | Musical quality | notes locked to the scale, voice-led chords, soft timbres, a real mix (limiter, about -16 to -18 LUFS), real musical form |
| 15% | Creative use of recursion | the call tree IS the musical form; recursion is visible (lens, code view, skyline) and audible (Wander/Bloom) |
| 10% | Visual design | bioluminescent tree, one coherent token system, 60 fps |
| 10% | Interaction & usability | moods, clear labels, keyboard shortcuts, share links |
| 5% | Technical execution | tests, CI, deploy, reliable export, clean architecture |

Mandatory deliverables (all must work in the deployed build): configurable recursion, interactive visualization, procedural music from the recursion, UI controls + playback, audio export, and a polished, accessible, relaxing experience.

## Stack (ask before changing)

Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript 7 (strict) · Tone.js 15 · Canvas 2D · Tailwind CSS 4 + CSS variables · Radix UI primitives · Zustand · Motion · Lucide icons · Fontsource fonts (Fraunces, Manrope, JetBrains Mono) · Vitest 5 + Testing Library · Playwright + @axe-core/playwright · oxlint + Prettier · GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages.

- Keep the create-vite defaults (oxlint, TypeScript 7). Do NOT add ESLint or typescript-eslint; typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7 yet.
- Tone.js v15: use `getTransport()`, `getDestination()`, `getDraw()`, `getContext()`. Never use the deprecated `Tone.Transport`, `Tone.Destination`, `Tone.Draw` or `Tone.context`.
- Unsure about a library API? Check Context7 (MCP) or the typings in `node_modules`. Never guess an API.
- Verify package versions with `npm view <pkg> version` before adding them.

## Commands

- `npm run dev` / `npm run build` / `npm run preview`
- `npm run verify`: typecheck + lint + unit tests + build. It must pass before every commit.
- `npm run test` (Vitest) · `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright: smoke, export, a11y)
- `npm run audio:qa`: renders reference seeds offline and checks peak, loudness and silence
- `npm run logs:collect`: copies every Claude Code transcript for this repo into `ai-logs/`

## Architecture rules

- One source of truth: `RecursionTrace` (pure) → `Score` (pure) → { live playback, offline export, MIDI, visuals }. Visuals and export never re-derive music.
- `src/core/**` is pure TypeScript: no DOM, no Tone.js, no React. It is deterministic for a given (params, seed) and fully unit-tested.
- `src/audio/**` owns Tone.js. ONE rack factory, `createRack(context, mood)`, serves BOTH live playback and `Tone.Offline` export.
- `src/viz/**` owns canvas rendering. It never schedules audio; it reacts to note events the scheduler emits through `getDraw()`.
- `src/ui/**` holds React components; state lives in `src/state` (Zustand). No business logic in components.
- Randomness only from the seeded PRNG in `src/core/random.ts`. `Math.random` is banned outside tests.
- New recursion worlds plug in through the `WorldDefinition` interface. Never special-case a world in audio or export code.

## Definition of done (every task)

1. `npm run verify` passes, and new logic has tests.
2. UI change: open the app with the Playwright MCP, take screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844, fix what looks off, and confirm zero console errors.
3. Audio change: tell the user exactly what to listen for. They are the ears; you cannot hear.
4. Accessibility: keyboard reachable, visible focus, real labels, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, nothing flashes more than 3 times a second.
5. Commit in small steps with conventional messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`).
6. End every turn with: what changed · how to see or hear it · known issues · the next step.

## Relaxation rules (never break)

- No sudden loud sounds. Every start, stop and change ramps: at least 50 ms against clicks, 1–3 s for scene changes. Master limiter at -1 dBTP.
- Notes are always quantised to the active scale. Default tempo 48–64 BPM. At most about 4 notes per second.
- Motion is slow: ambient loops last 6 s or longer, UI transitions 200–400 ms, no bounce, no shake, no flashing.
- Copy is short, warm and in the second person. No exclamation marks and no emoji in the UI.

# Seedsong: Recursive Soundscapes (Hub's Quest Epoch 1)

Solo 24-hour hackathon build. Hard deadline: **Thu 26 Nov 2026, 22:00 GMT+6**. Feature freeze: **18:30 GMT+6**.
Seedsong is a browser app where a recursive function grows a glowing fractal tree and the call tree itself becomes relaxing music.
The full product and technical spec is `docs/SPEC.md`. Read the section a task names before you start it. The official rubric and what a 10/10 looks like are in `docs/RUBRIC.md`.

## How we are judged (optimise in this order)

| Weight | Criterion | What it means for every decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 35% | Relaxation & UX | a calm first minute, no harsh sound or motion, frictionless controls, mobile works |
| 25% | Musical quality | notes locked to the scale, voice-led chords, soft timbres, a real mix (limiter, about -16 to -18 LUFS), real musical form |
| 15% | Creative use of recursion | the call tree IS the musical form; recursion is visible (lens, code view, skyline) and audible (Wander/Bloom) |
| 10% | Visual design | bioluminescent tree, one coherent token system, 60 fps |
| 10% | Interaction & usability | moods, clear labels, keyboard shortcuts, share links |
| 5% | Technical execution | tests, CI, deploy, reliable export, clean architecture |

Mandatory deliverables (all must work in the deployed build): configurable recursion, interactive visualization, procedural music from the recursion, UI controls + playback, audio export, and a polished, accessible, relaxing experience.

## Stack (ask before changing)

Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript 7 (strict) · Tone.js 15 · Canvas 2D · plain CSS design tokens (`src/styles/app.css`) with native accessible elements · Zustand · Lucide icons · Fontsource fonts (Fraunces, Manrope, JetBrains Mono) · @tonejs/midi · @breezystack/lamejs (MP3 worker) · Vitest 5 · Playwright + @axe-core/playwright (Microsoft Edge locally, Chromium in CI) · oxlint · GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages.

The build is DONE and verified (see README.md "Quality evidence" and `docs/DECISIONS.md` for every deviation from the spec: no Tailwind/Radix/Motion, no compose worker, dip-crossfade, a custom offline render loop). Work from here is polish, listening feedback and fixes, not re-scaffolding.

Node on this machine is a portable install: prefix shell commands with `export PATH="/c/Users/Tawfique/nodejs-portable/node-v26.13.1-win-x64:$PATH";` if `node` is not found.

- Keep the create-vite defaults (oxlint, TypeScript 7). Do NOT add ESLint or typescript-eslint; typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7 yet.
- Tone.js v15: use `getTransport()`, `getDestination()`, `getDraw()`, `getContext()`. Never use the deprecated `Tone.Transport`, `Tone.Destination`, `Tone.Draw` or `Tone.context`.
- Unsure about a library API? Check Context7 (MCP) or the typings in `node_modules`. Never guess an API.
- Verify package versions with `npm view <pkg> version` before adding them.

## Commands

- `npm run dev` / `npm run build` / `npm run preview`
- `npm run verify`: typecheck + lint + unit tests + build. It must pass before every commit.
- `npm run test` (Vitest) · `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright: smoke, export, a11y)
- `npm run audio:qa`: renders reference seeds offline and checks peak, loudness and silence
- `npm run logs:collect`: copies every Claude Code transcript for this repo into `ai-logs/`

## Architecture rules

- One source of truth: `RecursionTrace` (pure) → `Score` (pure) → { live playback, offline export, MIDI, visuals }. Visuals and export never re-derive music.
- `src/core/**` is pure TypeScript: no DOM, no Tone.js, no React. It is deterministic for a given (params, seed) and fully unit-tested.
- `src/audio/**` owns Tone.js. ONE rack factory, `createRack(context, mood)`, serves BOTH live playback and `Tone.Offline` export.
- `src/viz/**` owns canvas rendering. It never schedules audio; it reacts to note events the scheduler emits through `getDraw()`.
- `src/ui/**` holds React components; state lives in `src/state` (Zustand). No business logic in components.
- Randomness only from the seeded PRNG in `src/core/random.ts`. `Math.random` is banned outside tests.
- New recursion worlds plug in through the `WorldDefinition` interface. Never special-case a world in audio or export code.

## Definition of done (every task)

1. `npm run verify` passes, and new logic has tests.
2. UI change: open the app with the Playwright MCP, take screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844, fix what looks off, and confirm zero console errors.
3. Audio change: tell the user exactly what to listen for. They are the ears; you cannot hear.
4. Accessibility: keyboard reachable, visible focus, real labels, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, nothing flashes more than 3 times a second.
5. Commit in small steps with conventional messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`).
6. End every turn with: what changed · how to see or hear it · known issues · the next step.

## Relaxation rules (never break)

- No sudden loud sounds. Every start, stop and change ramps: at least 50 ms against clicks, 1–3 s for scene changes. Master limiter at -1 dBTP.
- Notes are always quantised to the active scale. Default tempo 48–64 BPM. At most about 4 notes per second.
- Motion is slow: ambient loops last 6 s or longer, UI transitions 200–400 ms, no bounce, no shake, no flashing.
- Copy is short, warm and in the second person. No exclamation marks and no emoji in the UI.

## Scope discipline

Follow the MoSCoW list in `docs/SPEC.md` §3. Never start a Could before every Must is done and verified. Ask before adding a dependency that is not listed above. After 18:30 GMT+6 only fixes, docs and polish.

content.text:
Your usage limit has been reached, so I'm stopping here. **Seedsong** is built, runs, and passes its checks. It's in `E:\UIU hackathon` and running at http://localhost:5173.

**What works:**
- **Two recursions you can shape:** Fractal Grove (`branch()`) and L-System Garden (`grow()`). The call tree becomes the music: each call is a note, each leaf (base case) a bell, and each return resolves a phrase.
- **Five moods**, plus Wander (depth-first) and Bloom (breadth-first) modes.
- **Visuals:** a glowing tree that grows in time with the music, blossoms on the leaves, a recursion lens showing the live call stack and the running line of code, and a "depth skyline" timeline you can click to jump around.
- **Export:** WAV, MP3, MIDI and cover art.
- **Relaxation tools:** a mixer for eight nature sounds, a breathing ring, sleep timer, zen mode, endless mode, share links and saved seeds.

**Test results:**
- `npm run verify` passes, including 24 unit tests. Generating and composing the biggest tree takes about 8 ms.
- End-to-end tests pass on desktop and phone sizes. Export downloads a real WAV, and passed 4 of 4 repeated runs after I fixed a timing bug.
- An automated accessibility checker found no serious problems on any screen.
- My loudness check renders all 5 moods in both modes: no distortion, no silent gaps, and the loudness is in the target range.
- Exporting a 3-minute song takes about a minute, with a real progress bar.

**Still to do:**
1. **Listen with headphones.** I can't hear the music. If something sounds harsh, muddy or busy, tell me in those words.
2. **Phone layout:** the "Keep this song" button overlaps the timeline. It's a small fix I didn't get to.
3. **Commit and publish:**
   - Nothing is committed yet. A git repo is set up on `main` with a `.gitignore`.
   - Create a public GitHub repo, push to it, then turn on Pages under Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
   - Add the live link and video link to `README.md`.
4. **Logs:** paste the planning chat's share link into `ai-logs/00-planning/planning-session.md`. Re-run `npm run logs:collect` before you submit. This session's log is already in `ai-logs/` (`INDEX.md`, `sessions/`, `transcripts/`).

- **Node.js:** it's a portable install in your user folder (`nodejs-portable`). Adding it to your PATH was blocked, so the kit's automatic logging won't work in new sessions until you add it.
- **Spec changes:** I dropped Tailwind, Radix and the third world (Hanoi), among others. Each deviation and the reason is in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
